title: Architect Quest
source: AWS Certified Solutions Architect Professional Slides v38(2).pdf
author: Stéphane Maarek

days.title: Identity, governance & security
days.mission: Jelaskan siapa boleh melakukan apa, lalu pilih preventive atau detective control yang tepat.
days.focus: IAM, STS, federation, Organizations, KMS, S3 security, WAF, threat detection
days.deliverable: Draw cross-account trust and explain 5 different security services without notes.

days.title: Trace the packet
days.mission: Ikuti request dari client sampai destination, termasuk DNS dan return path.
days.focus: VPC, NAT, endpoints, peering, TGW, VPN, Direct Connect, Resolver, Route 53, global routing
days.deliverable: Explain why a private EC2 instance can reach S3 but not the internet, then fix the right path.

days.title: Run, observe & release
days.mission: Pilih compute, scaling signal, deployment strategy, dan observability berdasarkan masalahnya.
days.focus: EC2, ECS/EKS, Lambda, load balancers, APIs, CloudWatch, CloudFormation, CodeDeploy, SSM
days.deliverable: Draw an application with its IAM roles, scaling signal, deployment rollback and logs.

days.title: Store, query & cache
days.mission: Bedakan file, block, object, relational, key-value, dan cache.
days.focus: EBS, EFS, FSx, S3, CloudFront, ElastiCache, DynamoDB, RDS, Aurora
days.deliverable: Choose storage/database for 6 workloads and reject the nearest alternative.

days.title: Events & analytics
days.mission: Bedakan queue, fan-out, replayable stream, delivery service, dan stateful processor.
days.focus: Step Functions, SQS, SNS, MQ, Kinesis, Firehose, Flink, MSK, Batch, EMR, Glue, Athena, Redshift
days.deliverable: Design a replayable ingestion pipeline and calculate its bottleneck.

days.title: Migrate, recover & control cost
days.mission: Tentukan migration path, data-loss tolerance, downtime target, dan cost trade-off.
days.focus: 7 Rs, Storage Gateway, DataSync, DMS, MGN, DRS, Backup, DR strategies, budgets and commitments
days.deliverable: Write a cutover and rollback plan with explicit RPO/RTO and data validation.

days.title: Complete the map
days.mission: Tutup topic gaps dan jelaskan keputusan, bukan sekadar nama service.
days.focus: AI/ML, CI/CD, WorkSpaces, AppStream, SES, Macie, IoT, worked sample cases and final recall
days.deliverable: Finish a mixed 25-question practice set and classify every mistake.

days.title: Repair weak mechanisms
days.mission: Fokus pada 3 pola kesalahan terbesar dari practice dan recall.
days.focus: Mistake queue, redrawn diagrams, focused scenario sets
days.deliverable: For each repaired error: explain the decisive constraint and why the distractor fails.

days.title: Timed practice & debrief
days.mission: Kerjakan fresh official practice atau gunakan 75-question session sebagai latihan pacing.
days.focus: 180-minute baseline session; then review every wrong or guessed response
days.deliverable: Create a one-page list of remaining knowledge gaps. Site score is not an AWS scaled score.

days.title: Final consolidation
days.mission: Review ringan: jargon, comparisons, correction notes dan high-value architectures.
days.focus: No broad new topics. Revisit mistakes and rehearse your question-reading routine.
days.deliverable: Explain IAM, DNS, DR, database replicas and messaging trade-offs without looking.

days.title: Exam window · final half-day
days.mission: Gunakan waktu tersisa untuk persiapan praktis dan recall ringan.
days.focus: Check booking details; use your actual permitted exam duration and follow the exam instructions.
days.deliverable: Read the objective, underline constraints, eliminate invalid answers, then choose the best fit.

lessons.title: How to think like a Professional architect
lessons.mental: SAP-C02 menguji pilihan terbaik di bawah constraints. Mengenal nama service saja belum cukup.
core: Read the business objective first: minimum downtime, least operational effort, lowest cost, or strict isolation.
Then identify hard constraints: protocol, engine compatibility, data residency, RPO/RTO, throughput, permissions, and team capacity.
Eliminate any answer that violates one hard constraint, even if its service is generally excellent. Compare the remaining options against the stated priority.
lessons.decision: Use a five-step routine: objective → constraints → mechanism → eliminate → trade-off.
lessons.trap: A familiar architecture is not automatically the best answer. “Managed” also does not mean you have no configuration responsibility.
lessons.example: A Windows application cannot simply move to Graviton because Graviton uses Arm processors and software compatibility matters.
lessons.question: Two answers work. How do you choose?
lessons.answer: Choose the one that meets every hard requirement and best satisfies the explicit optimization goal. Explain why the runner-up is worse.

lessons.title: IAM policies: who can do what?
lessons.mental: IAM = daftar izin. Principal adalah pihak yang meminta; action adalah kegiatan; resource adalah objek; condition adalah syarat.
core: Users can have long-lived credentials. Roles provide temporary credentials through STS. Groups organize users; roles are assumed, not joined.
A policy statement has Effect, Action/NotAction, Resource and optional Condition. Explicit deny wins. An absent allow is an implicit deny.
Managed policies can be reused; inline policies belong to one identity. Variables and principal/resource tags support ABAC.
lessons.decision: Use least privilege and roles for workloads. Conditions narrow a permission by context such as TLS, source network, region, tags or MFA.
lessons.trap: NotAction inside an Allow is not an explicit Deny. Another policy may allow an excluded action. Do not hard-code the changing contents of AWS managed policies.
lessons.example: Allow GetObject on reports/* plus Deny GetObject on reports/payroll/* means payroll remains denied. ListBucket needs the bucket ARN; object operations need an object ARN.
lessons.question: Does PowerUserAccess express an explicit denial of every IAM action?
lessons.answer: No. Its Allow with NotAction excludes actions from that statement. Read all policies and any explicit denies.

lessons.title: Roles, resource policies & permission ceilings
lessons.mental: Role = ganti kartu akses. Resource policy = pemilik pintu mengizinkan principal tertentu masuk. Boundary = batas maksimum.
core: Assuming a role creates a new session whose effective permissions come from the role and applicable restrictions; original user permissions are not added.
A resource policy is attached to a bucket, queue, key or other supported resource. Cross-account access normally needs permission on both sides.
A permissions boundary limits an identity; it grants nothing. Access Analyzer finds external access, validates policies and can generate policies from observed activity.
lessons.decision: Use a boundary when delegating IAM creation. Use a resource policy when granting access to a resource without switching the caller into a new role.
lessons.trap: Resource-policy behavior differs for user ARNs, role ARNs and assumed-role session ARNs. The simple “intersect everything” model is not universal; explicit denies still apply.
lessons.example: An analyst reads DynamoDB in account A and writes to S3 in B using its A role plus B bucket policy, avoiding an unnecessary role switch.
lessons.question: Can a boundary by itself grant s3:GetObject?
lessons.answer: No. It only limits permissions granted elsewhere. The appropriate allow and every applicable policy check are still required.

lessons.title: STS, cross-account access & confused deputy
lessons.mental: STS = loket yang menerbitkan kartu akses sementara. Trust policy menjawab siapa boleh assume role.
core: AssumeRole needs a role trust relationship and caller authorization. The returned access key, secret key and session token belong together.
For a third-party provider serving many customers, require a unique ExternalId in the trust policy. The provider supplies the customer-specific value when assuming the role.
AssumeRoleWithSAML and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity exchange federation assertions/tokens. Session tags carry attributes into authorization.
lessons.decision: Deploy least-privilege monitoring roles to member accounts with StackSets. Trust the provider account and require its ExternalId.
lessons.trap: ExternalId is not a password or secret. Its purpose is preventing customer A from tricking a provider into accessing customer B. Role chaining has a one-hour session limit.
lessons.example: A vendor knows many customer role ARNs. AWS checks both its principal and the ExternalId, binding the request to the intended customer.
lessons.question: Why is trusting only the vendor account insufficient?
lessons.answer: All of that vendor’s customer requests may originate from the same account. ExternalId distinguishes the customer on whose behalf it acts.

lessons.title: Federation: SAML, OIDC & Cognito
lessons.mental: Federation = login di identity provider, lalu AWS mempercayai bukti login tersebut. Tidak perlu IAM user per orang.
core: SAML 2.0 commonly federates enterprise identities. STS AssumeRoleWithSAML returns temporary credentials for API access; console federation adds AWS sign-in redirection.
OIDC uses web identity tokens. Cognito user pools authenticate application users and issue JWTs; identity pools exchange supported identity tokens for temporary AWS credentials.
A custom identity broker authenticates with a legacy identity system and obtains scoped temporary credentials when standard federation is unavailable.
lessons.decision: Workforce across AWS accounts: IAM Identity Center. Customer application login: Cognito user pool. Customer direct S3 access: identity pool plus role permissions.
lessons.trap: A user-pool JWT is not an AWS access key. Direct OIDC federation also has valid workload uses; “always use Cognito” is too broad.
lessons.example: A mobile app signs in to a user pool, presents its JWT to API Gateway, or uses an identity pool for restricted direct uploads to a user prefix.
lessons.question: Which Cognito pool gives AWS credentials?
lessons.answer: Identity pools. User pools primarily provide application authentication and tokens.

lessons.title: Active Directory: managed, proxy, or basic?
lessons.mental: AD menyimpan identitas dan domain objects. ADFS menerbitkan federation assertions. Keduanya punya tugas berbeda.
core: AWS Managed Microsoft AD supplies managed domain controllers, multi-AZ availability and supported integrations such as domain join and RDS SQL Server. Trust can connect it to on-premises AD.
AD Connector proxies authentication to existing on-premises AD. It does not cache credentials or create a new directory replica; connectivity remains a dependency.
Simple AD is a smaller Samba-based compatible directory without Microsoft AD’s full feature set or forest trust.
lessons.decision: Need Microsoft AD features/trust: Managed Microsoft AD. Keep identities only on premises and proxy authentication: AD Connector. Basic standalone compatibility: Simple AD.
lessons.trap: A forest trust does not copy users. AD Connector does not keep authentication working through a lost on-premises connection.
lessons.example: For resilient AD access, plan DNS, network redundancy and domain-controller availability; merely creating a trust does not remove network dependencies.
lessons.question: Trust versus replication: what changes?
lessons.answer: Trust permits authentication across domains. Replication copies directory data among appropriate domain controllers.

lessons.title: Organizations & multi-account structure
lessons.mental: AWS account adalah isolation boundary untuk resources, permissions, billing attribution, dan banyak quotas. OU mengelompokkan accounts.
core: Separate production, development, security and log archive accounts according to risk and ownership. OUs organize common controls.
Organizations supports consolidated billing and all-features governance. Discount sharing can pool eligible RI and Savings Plans benefits; it can also be disabled.

OrganizationAccountAccessRole is created for accounts created through Organizations; invited accounts need an appropriate role established separately. Moving an account requires leaving/removal from its current organization before joining another.
lessons.decision: Use accounts for strong workload/administrative isolation; use VPCs for network separation inside an account. Centralize logs in a dedicated account.
lessons.trap: Consolidated billing does not grant cross-account resource access. A management-account role is not automatically an administrator of every resource in every member account.
lessons.example: Finance receives one bill, while production operators and development operators retain separate role assignments and account quotas.
lessons.question: Why not put every team in one account with separate VPCs?
lessons.answer: VPCs separate networks, but they do not provide the same IAM, billing and account-level quota boundaries as separate accounts.

lessons.title: SCPs, tags & organization policies
lessons.mental: SCP = pagar organisasi. IAM masih harus memberikan izin di dalam pagar itu.
core: SCPs constrain member-account principals, including their root users. They do not constrain the management account or service-linked roles.
An allow must survive every level along the OU path; an explicit deny at any applicable level blocks access. Use aws:RequestedRegion carefully because global services need exceptions.
Tag policies standardize supported tags; enforce required tag presence with suitable request-tag conditions/SCPs. Organization backup and AI opt-out policies centralize their respective settings.
lessons.decision: Use preventive controls for prohibited actions. Use tag policies for consistency and separate checks for missing required tags.
lessons.trap: ForAllValues on aws:TagKeys validates supplied keys; it does not prove every required tag exists. Missing-value/Null conditions matter. Tag policies do not universally stop untagged resources.
lessons.example: A developer has AdministratorAccess, but a parent OU denies ec2:RunInstances outside approved Regions. The launch fails.
lessons.question: Does attaching FullAWSAccess as an SCP grant admin access?
lessons.answer: No. It removes that SCP restriction; an identity still needs its own permissions.

lessons.title: IAM Identity Center & permission sets
lessons.mental: Satu workforce login, akses berbeda untuk setiap AWS account. Permission set adalah paket izin yang diprovisikan menjadi role.
core: Connect an identity source: built-in directory, supported external IdP or AD. Assign users/groups to accounts with permission sets.
The same engineer can have ReadOnly in production and Administrator in a sandbox. Attribute-based access control can map workforce attributes to session tags.
Application assignments enable SAML application access; they are distinct from permissions to AWS resources.
lessons.decision: Choose Identity Center for centralized workforce access across accounts. Use roles for machine-to-machine vendor access.
lessons.trap: Sharing a human username/password with a monitoring vendor is a poor machine identity design. A permission set must be assigned to the right account and principal.
lessons.example: Group Developers receives DeveloperAccess in Dev and ReadOnly in Prod; Operators receives a separate production operations permission set.
lessons.question: What is the difference between identity source and permission set?
lessons.answer: The source authenticates who you are; the permission set determines the AWS access you receive in assigned accounts.

lessons.title: Control Tower: a governed landing zone
lessons.mental: Landing zone = lingkungan AWS awal yang sudah punya struktur accounts, logging, identity, dan controls.
core: Control Tower orchestrates a governed multi-account environment on top of Organizations. Account Factory automates account provisioning with approved baselines.
Preventive controls stop actions, detective controls report noncompliance, and proactive controls can check supported resources before provisioning.
Mandatory, strongly recommended and elective describe guidance levels, not whether a control is preventive or detective.
lessons.decision: Choose Control Tower when asked to quickly establish and consistently govern a new multi-account environment.
lessons.trap: AWS Config detecting a violation is not the same as an SCP blocking it. Account Factory provisions baselines; it does not design every application.
lessons.example: A new project account inherits logging and organization controls automatically instead of a team manually rebuilding them each time.
lessons.question: Which control can stop a prohibited API action before it happens?
lessons.answer: An appropriate preventive control such as an SCP. Detective Config rules evaluate state after creation/change.

lessons.title: RAM: share infrastructure without merging ownership
lessons.mental: RAM = berbagi resource yang didukung, bukan berbagi semua izin atau semua data dalam account.
core: VPC subnet sharing lets participant accounts launch their own resources into centrally managed subnets. Network owners manage routing; participants retain ownership of their resources.
Share supported resources such as Transit Gateways, Resolver rules, managed prefix lists and private CAs to reduce duplication.
Customer-managed prefix lists group CIDRs, letting one maintained list feed multiple security rules. Sharing Resolver rules centralizes hybrid DNS forwarding.
lessons.decision: Use RAM when the requirement says shared subnets, shared TGW or common DNS rules across accounts.
lessons.trap: Connectivity still depends on route tables, security groups and NACLs. Shared subnet does not mean unrestricted access or ownership of another account’s instances.
lessons.example: A networking account owns subnets and TGW; app accounts deploy services into shared subnets and manage only their own workloads.
lessons.question: RAM or Organizations for consolidated billing?
lessons.answer: Organizations handles consolidated billing. RAM shares supported resources.

lessons.title: CloudTrail: who changed it?
lessons.mental: CloudTrail adalah audit trail API activity. CloudWatch menjawab kesehatan; Config menjawab konfigurasi.
core: Management events describe control-plane changes such as launching EC2. Data events describe supported resource-level operations such as S3 GetObject and require appropriate configuration.
Event history provides recent management events. Trails or other configured storage support longer retention; central multi-account logging needs the right destination policies.

Use EventBridge for event-driven reactions, CloudWatch metric filters for repeated patterns, and S3/Athena for durable analysis. Integrity validation detects tampering; Object Lock can protect retention.
lessons.decision: Deleted resource or suspicious API action: CloudTrail. Organization-wide audit retention: organization trail plus a protected log archive.
lessons.trap: CloudTrail is not a SQL query log, packet capture or hard real-time prevention system. A trail and 90-day event history are not the same feature.
lessons.example: An alarm counts repeated denied API calls; responders inspect the initiating role and source context in CloudTrail.
lessons.question: How do you audit S3 object downloads?
lessons.answer: Configure relevant S3 object data events. Default management-event history alone is insufficient.

lessons.title: KMS & envelope encryption
lessons.mental: Envelope encryption = kunci data mengenkripsi data; KMS key melindungi kunci data itu.
core: Customer-managed keys offer policies, lifecycle control and auditing. AWS managed and AWS owned keys give progressively less customer control.
Imported key material keeps external material-management responsibilities with you. A custom key store uses your CloudHSM cluster. Key origin and algorithm affect supported rotation features.

Related multi-Region keys share key material and key ID but have regional ARNs, policies and independent regional management. Services do not automatically become globally replicated because their keys are related.
lessons.decision: Use a customer-managed key when cross-account sharing or custom controls are required. Check both IAM permissions and key policy.
lessons.trap: S3 read permission does not imply kms:Decrypt. Key rotation does not re-encrypt every existing object; old ciphertext must remain decryptable.
lessons.example: An S3 reader in account B needs the bucket/object permission and permission to decrypt with the customer-managed key in A.
lessons.question: Does a multi-Region KMS key replicate my S3 objects?
lessons.answer: No. It addresses cryptographic interoperability; configure data replication independently.

lessons.title: Parameter Store vs Secrets Manager
lessons.mental: Parameter = konfigurasi. Secret = nilai sensitif yang perlu lifecycle dan sering perlu rotation.
core: Parameter Store provides hierarchical names, versions and optional SecureString encryption. Advanced parameter policies include expiration and notifications; expiration is not password rotation.
Secrets Manager provides managed secret storage, resource policies and supported rotation workflows. Rotating a database secret must coordinate the stored value and the database password.
A secret injected into a container environment at startup is a snapshot. Rotation does not magically rewrite running process variables.
lessons.decision: Simple configuration: Parameter Store. Database credentials requiring managed rotation: Secrets Manager. Cross-account secret access: resource policy plus KMS permissions.
lessons.trap: Encrypting a value is not rotating it. A cached or injected secret can become stale after rotation.
lessons.example: Store /shop/prod/api-url as a parameter and the production database password as a rotating secret. Refresh clients or redeploy tasks as needed.
lessons.question: Why can a container fail after successful secret rotation?
lessons.answer: Its environment may still contain the old credential. Applications must refresh secrets or tasks must be replaced.

lessons.title: TLS, certificates, SNI & ACM
lessons.mental: TLS melindungi data saat bergerak. Sertifikat membuktikan identitas server; encryption at rest melindungi penyimpanan.
core: Modern TLS negotiates symmetric session keys using secure handshake mechanisms. Validate the certificate chain and hostname; using HTTPS while trusting a malicious certificate defeats protection.
SNI tells the server which hostname the client wants, allowing multiple certificates on a listener.

ACM manages certificates for supported integrations. CloudFront viewer certificates belong in us-east-1; regional load balancers use regional certificates. Imported certificates require renewal handling.
lessons.decision: Terminate TLS at ALB for managed certificate integration; use HTTPS to targets too when end-to-end encryption is required.
lessons.trap: DNSSEC authenticates DNS data; it does not encrypt application traffic. The deck’s legacy RSA handshake is not a universal description of modern TLS.
lessons.example: shop.example.com and api.example.com share an ALB HTTPS listener with SNI choosing the relevant certificate.
lessons.question: Does TLS termination on ALB guarantee encryption to EC2?
lessons.answer: No. Configure HTTPS between ALB and targets if that leg must also be encrypted.

lessons.title: CloudHSM & TLS architecture
lessons.mental: CloudHSM memberi dedicated hardware cryptography dengan tanggung jawab key/user administration di pihak kamu.
core: KMS is managed key usage through AWS APIs and policies. CloudHSM offers dedicated HSMs and cryptographic interfaces for applications with specific control requirements.
Deploy HSMs across AZs for availability. Applications need supported client integration and cryptographic-user access, not just IAM permission to create a cluster.
TLS offload can keep private-key operations inside the HSM while servers handle application traffic.
lessons.decision: Choose CloudHSM when dedicated HSM control or specific cryptographic interfaces are mandatory. Choose KMS for simpler service-integrated key management.
lessons.trap: Buying one HSM does not produce multi-AZ resilience. Also, CloudHSM user credentials and IAM administration solve different access layers.
lessons.example: A regulated service uses an NLB TCP listener and web servers integrated with a multi-AZ CloudHSM cluster for private-key operations.
lessons.question: Who manages cryptographic users in CloudHSM?
lessons.answer: You manage HSM users and keys; AWS manages the underlying hardware service.

lessons.title: S3 security, signed access & WORM
lessons.mental: S3 authorization, encryption, network path, dan retention adalah empat lapisan yang berbeda.
core: SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys; SSE-KMS adds KMS control/audit; SSE-C supplies customer keys with requests; client-side encryption happens before upload.
Bucket policies, IAM policies, Block Public Access and Object Ownership govern access. A presigned URL delegates a specific signed operation and expires no later than its signing credentials.
Object Lock protects object versions. Governance mode can be bypassed with authorized permissions; compliance retention cannot be shortened during its protected period. Legal holds are separate.
lessons.decision: Use presigned uploads to let clients send large objects directly to S3. Use compliance retention for strict immutable records.
lessons.trap: Presigned URL is a bearer capability, not a new IAM identity. Default encryption does not by itself deny uploads using an unwanted encryption choice.
lessons.example: An authenticated app issues a short-lived PUT URL for one exact object key; the client uploads directly instead of passing a large file through API Gateway.
lessons.question: Does a bucket-level permission use the same ARN as an object-level permission?
lessons.answer: No. ListBucket targets the bucket ARN; GetObject/PutObject target object ARNs such as bucket/prefix/*.

lessons.title: S3 access points & multi-Region access
lessons.mental: Access point = pintu bernama dengan policy tersendiri untuk dataset yang sama.
core: Use access points to separate team access by prefix or application. A VPC-only access point also needs an appropriate VPC endpoint and policies.
Multi-Region Access Points route through a global endpoint to regional buckets. Replication and failover controls are separate decisions; do not assume routing copies the data.
S3 Object Lambda transforms content during retrieval in the slide architecture. Its availability for new customers has changed; keep the pattern distinct from a new deployment recommendation.
lessons.decision: Many teams sharing one bucket: access points. Global bucket routing with controlled failover: MRAP plus designed replication.
lessons.trap: “Nearest bucket” is useful only if the required object exists there. Asynchronous replication permits lag.
lessons.example: Finance gets a /finance access point; analytics gets read-only access. Both use the same bucket while retaining different policies.
lessons.question: If MRAP is created, are all historical objects automatically replicated?
lessons.answer: No. Configure replication and address existing objects separately, for example with supported batch replication.

lessons.title: WAF, Shield & Firewall Manager
lessons.mental: WAF memeriksa HTTP requests; Shield menghadapi DDoS; Firewall Manager menyebarkan policies secara terpusat.
core: Shield Standard provides baseline protection; Advanced adds supported enhanced protections and response capabilities. WAF handles L7 rules, managed rule groups, IP sets and rate-based controls.
CloudFront and Route 53 distribute exposure at the edge. Protect origins too: VPC origins or restricted network access plus appropriately protected origin headers where applicable.
Use Firewall Manager for consistent supported security policies across organization accounts.
lessons.decision: SQL injection or HTTP abuse: WAF. Large DDoS requirements: Shield strategy. Consistency across accounts: Firewall Manager.
lessons.trap: WAF can help mitigate application-layer DDoS; “WAF is not for DDoS” is too absolute. An ALB’s client-facing HTTP identity differs from the network peer seen behind CloudFront.
lessons.example: Block a malicious viewer IP at WAF on CloudFront. Blocking a CloudFront edge IP at the origin could block many legitimate users.
lessons.question: Does a security group have a deny rule?
lessons.answer: No. SGs allow traffic. Use the appropriate NACL, WAF or firewall for explicit blocking at the relevant layer.

lessons.title: Inspector, Config & GuardDuty
lessons.mental: Vulnerability, compliance, dan threat detection bukan hal yang sama.
core: Inspector finds supported workload vulnerabilities, including relevant EC2, container and Lambda findings.
Config records resource configuration and evaluates compliance. Rules can invoke remediation using Systems Manager; configuration recording alone does not prevent a change.
GuardDuty analyzes supported telemetry for suspicious activity. Delegated administration supports organization-wide management; findings can trigger EventBridge response workflows.
lessons.decision: Known vulnerable package: Inspector. Public security group violates policy: Config. Compromised instance behavior: GuardDuty.
lessons.trap: A detective finding is evidence to investigate, not proof that automated destructive remediation is always appropriate. Do not confuse a Config aggregator with a recorder in every account.
lessons.example: An instance contacting a suspicious destination triggers GuardDuty; its vulnerable package appears in Inspector; its open SSH rule appears in Config.
lessons.question: Which service answers “how did this security group change over time”?
lessons.answer: AWS Config for configuration history, with CloudTrail to identify the API caller.

lessons.title: Security investigation & access context
lessons.mental: Conditions mempersempit izin berdasarkan konteks. Security Hub mengumpulkan findings; Detective membantu investigasi.
core: Use aws:PrincipalOrgID in a resource policy to constrain access to organization members, alongside required permissions.
SourceIp, SourceVpc and SourceVpce describe different paths. For endpoint requests, use the correct context keys rather than assuming the public-source-IP key applies.
EC2 Instance Connect pushes short-lived SSH keys but still requires SSH connectivity for that connection mode. Security Hub centralizes findings; Detective builds investigation context.
lessons.decision: Need shell access without opening inbound SSH: Session Manager. Need correlated findings: Security Hub. Need root-cause context: Detective.
lessons.trap: CloudTrail logging StartSession is not the same as recording every command. SSH/port-forwarded Session Manager traffic has session-content logging limitations.
lessons.example: A resource policy trusts only the organization, while a separate IAM role limits which objects the responder may inspect.
lessons.question: Security Hub or Detective for aggregating security findings?
lessons.answer: Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings. Detective helps investigate relationships and suspicious activity.

lessons.title: EC2, placement & high-performance computing
lessons.mental: Pilih compute dari bottleneck: CPU, RAM, I/O, GPU, atau komunikasi antar-node.
core: General-purpose, compute, memory, storage and accelerated families serve different workload shapes. Graviton requires compatible Arm software.
Cluster placement favors low-latency communication in one AZ. Spread reduces correlated hardware failure; partition placement separates groups of racks for distributed systems.
ENA improves networking; EFA supports tightly coupled HPC. Pair appropriate compute with FSx for Lustre, EBS or local scratch, and use Batch/ParallelCluster for orchestration.
lessons.decision: Low-latency MPI job: cluster placement plus supported EFA instances. Rack-aware distributed data: partition placement. Independent critical nodes: spread.
lessons.trap: A cluster placement group optimizes locality, not multi-AZ availability. RAM is not a default EC2 CloudWatch metric; install an agent.
lessons.example: A simulation uses EFA nodes and Lustre for parallel input while durable results go to S3. Local scratch can be lost and regenerated.
lessons.question: Which placement group deliberately separates rack partitions?
lessons.answer: Partition placement. The application can use partition information to distribute replicas.

lessons.title: Auto Scaling: match demand without instability
lessons.mental: Scaling menambah capacity; health replacement mengganti resource rusak. Dua mekanisme berbeda.
core: Target tracking maintains a utilization target; step policies respond to alarm bands; scheduled scaling anticipates known peaks; predictive scaling forecasts patterns.
Lifecycle hooks pause launch/termination for preparation or cleanup. Instance Refresh replaces instances using a new launch-template version while respecting health/warm-up settings.

Use an application-relevant metric: queue backlog per worker, requests per target, CPU or another real bottleneck. Health checks should identify unhealthy instances without triggering mass replacement because a shared dependency fails.
lessons.decision: Select the scaling signal that tracks per-instance demand and allow realistic warm-up time.
lessons.trap: Changing an AMI in a template does not modify existing instances. A database outage should not cause every healthy web server to be endlessly replaced.
lessons.example: At 120 requests/s and a target of 30 per instance, approximately four ready instances are needed, subject to headroom and workload behavior.
lessons.question: What does Instance Refresh solve?
lessons.answer: It rolls existing ASG instances onto a new template/configuration; editing the template alone affects future launches.

lessons.title: Spot & purchase models
lessons.mental: Spot = capacity murah yang boleh diambil kembali. Desain harus tahan interruption.
core: Use checkpointing, retryable tasks and diversified instance types/AZs. Price-capacity-optimized allocation balances available capacity and price.
On-Demand handles flexible reliable baseline needs. Savings Plans and RIs exchange commitment for billing discounts. Dedicated Hosts offer physical host control useful for certain licenses.
A mixed ASG or fleet can maintain an On-Demand baseline while using Spot for expendable workers.
lessons.decision: Fault-tolerant batch or stateless workers: consider Spot. Non-interruptible stateful singleton: do not rely solely on Spot.
lessons.trap: Spot interruption can result from capacity needs, not just price. A billing discount is not always a capacity reservation.
lessons.example: Video chunks are independent, checkpointed and queued; interrupted workers are replaced and unacknowledged chunks retry.
lessons.question: Does Reserved Instance mean a special VM image?
lessons.answer: No. It is primarily a purchasing/billing construct, with capacity-reservation behavior depending on the reservation scope.

lessons.title: ECS, Fargate & ECR
lessons.mental: ECR menyimpan image; ECS menjadwalkan tasks; Fargate menjalankan containers tanpa kamu mengelola EC2 hosts.
core: Task definition describes containers, resources and networking. A task is a running copy; a service maintains the desired task count.
Separate the task role (application AWS API access), task execution role (platform actions such as pulling images/secrets), and EC2 instance role where used.
awsvpc gives tasks their own networking/SGs. Bridge-mode EC2 tasks can use dynamic port mapping. Scale services and underlying EC2 capacity appropriately; Fargate removes host-capacity management.
lessons.decision: Minimum container-host operations: ECS on Fargate. Need host control or specialized EC2 options: ECS on EC2.
lessons.trap: Image scanning finds vulnerabilities; it does not patch the image. A rotated injected secret requires a refresh strategy. Task scaling alone does not add EC2 host capacity.
lessons.example: A task writes invoices to S3 using its task role; its execution role lets ECS pull the image from ECR and inject the startup secret.
lessons.question: Which role grants application code access to DynamoDB?
lessons.answer: The ECS task role, scoped to the table and required actions.

lessons.title: EKS & containers outside AWS
lessons.mental: EKS memakai Kubernetes APIs; ECS memakai AWS-native orchestration. Pilih berdasarkan kebutuhan platform yang nyata.
core: EKS manages the Kubernetes control plane. Managed node groups simplify EC2 node management; self-managed nodes give more control; Fargate fits supported pod workloads.
Storage uses CSI drivers and compatible StorageClasses. An EBS volume is AZ-bound; EFS provides shared NFS access across AZs where supported.
ECS Anywhere extends AWS-managed ECS scheduling to external infrastructure with agents. EKS Anywhere runs Kubernetes on customer-managed infrastructure with its own operational model.
lessons.decision: Existing Kubernetes skills, manifests and ecosystem requirements favor EKS. A simple container requirement alone does not require Kubernetes.
lessons.trap: Container images are not automatically portable across every OS/CPU. A managed control plane does not eliminate application, pod, node or network responsibilities.
lessons.example: A company moves existing Kubernetes workloads to EKS, checks CSI and networking compatibility, and retains Kubernetes deployment workflows.
lessons.question: Is ECS Anywhere the same as EKS Anywhere?
lessons.answer: No. ECS Anywhere extends ECS control to external hosts; EKS Anywhere is Kubernetes deployed outside AWS with a different control/operations model.

lessons.title: Lambda: invocation, concurrency & networking
lessons.mental: Lambda menjalankan functions saat ada trigger. Concurrency adalah jumlah executions yang berjalan bersamaan.
core: Synchronous callers receive the result and handle invocation retries. Asynchronous invocation queues events and has retry/destination controls. SQS uses event-source polling with queue semantics.
Reserved concurrency caps and reserves function concurrency; provisioned concurrency keeps environments prepared to reduce startup latency.
VPC-attached Lambda can reach private databases. Internet egress needs a working route through NAT; placing it in a public subnet does not give it a public IP.
lessons.decision: Short event-driven work: Lambda. Use SQS and controlled concurrency to protect a slow downstream service.
lessons.trap: One standard invocation is limited to 15 minutes. At 1,769 MB the CPU equivalent is one vCPU. Lambda concurrency is not requests per second.
lessons.example: 100 requests/s × 0.2 seconds average duration ≈ 20 concurrent executions. NAT with an EIP gives external APIs a fixed outbound IP.
lessons.question: How can a Lambda call a private RDS instance and a public API?
lessons.answer: Attach it to appropriate private subnets/SGs; use private connectivity to RDS and a NAT route for the public API.

lessons.title: ALB, NLB & GWLB
lessons.mental: ALB memahami HTTP; NLB mengarahkan network flows; GWLB memasukkan security appliances ke jalur traffic.
core: ALB supports host/path/header routing and targets such as instances, IPs and Lambda. NLB serves supported TCP/UDP/TLS workloads with static zonal addresses.
GWLB distributes encapsulated traffic to inspection appliances using GENEVE. Route design must steer traffic through the inspection path.
Cross-zone balancing spreads traffic across AZ targets. Stickiness may preserve affinity but cause imbalance; external session storage supports stateless application tiers.
lessons.decision: HTTP path routing: ALB. Static IP plus TCP/UDP: NLB. Third-party transparent inspection fleet: GWLB.
lessons.trap: ALB supports mutual TLS. Cross-zone can be disabled at supported ALB target groups, so the slide’s “always on, cannot disable” is incomplete.
lessons.example: Two AZs contain 2 and 8 targets. With equal zonal ingress, disabling cross-zone produces much more traffic per target in the smaller AZ.
lessons.question: Does NLB use HTTP path rules?
lessons.answer: No. If static IPs and ALB HTTP routing are both needed, a supported NLB-to-ALB architecture can combine them.

lessons.title: API Gateway: management, security & limits
lessons.mental: API Gateway adalah front door API dengan authentication, throttling, stages dan integrations.
core: Use direct AWS service integration when no custom Lambda logic is needed. Stages separate deployed versions; caching and usage plans are API-type-specific features.

IAM SigV4, Cognito/JWT and Lambda authorizers solve authentication/authorization. API keys meter usage; they are not strong authentication. CORS is a browser-enforced cross-origin permission mechanism.
Diagnose 4xx/5xx with gateway and integration metrics/logs. A 502 alone does not prove a concurrency problem.
lessons.decision: Large uploads: generate a presigned S3 URL. Public API with auth/throttling: API Gateway. Simple mixed HTTP targets: ALB may suffice.
lessons.trap: The 29-second integration timeout is not universal: some Regional/private REST APIs support quota increases. Distinguish REST, HTTP and WebSocket API features.
lessons.example: A 100 MB upload bypasses the gateway payload ceiling by going from client directly to S3 after an authorized URL request.
lessons.question: Why is enabling CORS on S3 insufficient for a browser calling an API?
lessons.answer: The API response must permit the web page’s origin; configure CORS on the API endpoint being called.

lessons.title: WebSockets & AppSync GraphQL
lessons.mental: WebSocket mempertahankan koneksi dua arah. GraphQL menentukan data yang diminta dan resolvers yang mengambilnya.
core: API Gateway WebSockets manage connection events and route messages. Store connection IDs if the backend needs to send messages through the connection-management API.
AppSync resolves GraphQL fields against supported data sources or Lambda and supports real-time application patterns.
Authentication to Cognito is separate from resolver IAM permission to read the backing data source.
lessons.decision: Real-time bidirectional messaging with custom routes: WebSocket API. Unified GraphQL access to multiple data sources: AppSync.
lessons.trap: An authenticated user must still be authorized for a particular operation or record. GraphQL does not remove the need to design access control.
lessons.example: A delivery dashboard subscribes to order-status updates while a resolver reads order details from DynamoDB.
lessons.question: Does AppSync replace DynamoDB?
lessons.answer: No. It is an API layer that uses data sources such as DynamoDB, Aurora, HTTP endpoints or Lambda.

lessons.title: Route 53: records & routing choices
lessons.mental: DNS menjawab alamat tujuan. Setelah jawaban di-cache, client mungkin belum melihat perubahan berikutnya.
core: A/AAAA map to IPv4/IPv6. CNAME aliases another hostname but not the zone apex. Route 53 Alias supports selected targets and apex records.
Weighted routing distributes DNS answers by weights; latency chooses measured regional latency; geolocation uses user geography; geoproximity includes bias; IP-based routing uses CIDR mappings.
Failover chooses primary/secondary health-based records. Multivalue returns several healthy answers; it is not a replacement for a load balancer.
lessons.decision: Canary by DNS: weighted. Lowest regional latency: latency. Country-specific answer: geolocation. Simple active/passive recovery: failover.
lessons.trap: Weighted DNS is not an exact percentage of HTTP requests because resolvers and clients cache responses. Lower TTL speeds change visibility but increases DNS queries.
lessons.example: A resolver caches a blue-environment address for 300 seconds; a DNS swap does not immediately move every existing client.
lessons.question: Can an Alias point directly at an arbitrary EC2 public DNS name?
lessons.answer: No. Alias supports specific target types; use an appropriate A record or other valid DNS design.

lessons.title: DNS health, hosted zones & failover
lessons.mental: Public hosted zone untuk internet DNS; private hosted zone untuk associated VPCs. Health check menentukan availability signal.
core: Public health checkers cannot directly reach private-only endpoints. Publish a suitable CloudWatch metric/alarm and use an alarm-based health check for private resources.
Calculated checks combine health signals. Ensure health checks represent service readiness and allow checker traffic where required.
DNSSEC authenticates DNS data. Private hosted zone resolution requires appropriate VPC DNS settings and associations.
lessons.decision: Private database failover signal: custom metric/alarm plus controlled promotion and DNS updates.
lessons.trap: Changing DNS does not promote a read replica, synchronize lost writes or repair application connection pools. Those are separate recovery steps.
lessons.example: An automated runbook verifies primary failure, promotes the replica, changes the application endpoint and validates writes in the recovery region.
lessons.question: Can Route 53 endpoint health checks reach 10.0.1.10 directly?
lessons.answer: No. Use a reachable health endpoint or an alarm-based signal derived from inside the private environment.

lessons.title: Hybrid DNS: inbound vs outbound Resolver
lessons.mental: Arah endpoint dilihat dari sisi AWS: inbound = masuk AWS, outbound = keluar AWS menuju DNS kamu.
core: Inbound endpoints let on-premises resolvers query AWS private DNS. Outbound endpoints send matching VPC DNS queries to on-premises DNS servers.
Forwarding rules define domains and target DNS servers; more specific matching rules win. System rules can override forwarding for selected namespaces.
Deploy endpoint IPs across AZs, permit DNS traffic, provide VPN/DX routing and share Resolver rules with RAM where appropriate.
lessons.decision: On-premises asks for an AWS private name: inbound. EC2 asks for an internal corporate name: outbound.
lessons.trap: A network connection alone does not create conditional DNS forwarding. Do not forward every domain both ways and accidentally create a loop.
lessons.example: EC2 asks payroll.corp.internal; the outbound rule forwards only corp.internal to the corporate DNS over a private network path.
lessons.question: What is shared centrally to reuse outbound forwarding across accounts?
lessons.answer: Supported Route 53 Resolver rules through AWS RAM, associated with the consuming VPCs.

lessons.title: Global entry points & architecture selection
lessons.mental: Tentukan apakah masalahnya caching, global routing, DNS, atau compute scaling.
core: CloudFront caches content and accelerates HTTP delivery. Global Accelerator routes supported TCP/UDP traffic over AWS’s network using stable anycast addresses and endpoint health.

An EIP on one instance provides a fixed address but is not a scalable multi-AZ architecture. ALB+ASG adds health routing and horizontal capacity; containers or Lambda alter the compute operating model.
API Gateway direct integration removes unnecessary Lambda code for supported service-proxy tasks.
lessons.decision: Static global addresses or non-HTTP acceleration: Global Accelerator. Cacheable HTTP content: CloudFront. API policies: API Gateway.
lessons.trap: Global Accelerator does not cache objects. CloudFront is not merely static-only. Neither removes database failover or downstream-capacity constraints.
lessons.example: A UDP game uses Global Accelerator; its web assets use CloudFront/S3; purchase APIs use API Gateway with appropriate authentication.
lessons.question: Why put API Gateway directly in front of SQS?
lessons.answer: When the request only needs authorized message submission, direct integration avoids an unnecessary Lambda hop and its operations/cost.

lessons.title: Outposts, Local Zones & Wavelength
lessons.mental: AWS Region diperluas ke lokasi yang berbeda untuk alasan latency atau data placement.
core: Outposts puts selected AWS infrastructure/services in customer premises, with physical-site responsibilities and a regional service connection.
Local Zones put selected AWS services nearer metropolitan users while remaining associated with a parent Region.
Wavelength places supported infrastructure within telecom networks for suitable low-latency applications. Service and location availability vary.
lessons.decision: Data must stay in your own facility: consider Outposts. Metro proximity: Local Zones. Telecom-edge use case: Wavelength.
lessons.trap: “AWS-like experience on premises” does not make every AWS service available locally or every workload disconnected-capable.
lessons.example: A factory processes latency-sensitive data on Outposts and sends permitted aggregated results to its parent Region.
lessons.question: Which option is installed in a customer’s data center?
lessons.answer: AWS Outposts.

lessons.title: EBS, snapshots & instance store
lessons.mental: Block storage terlihat seperti disk. EBS persistent melalui network; instance store menempel pada host dan bersifat ephemeral.
core: Choose gp3 for typical general-purpose SSD workloads; provisioned-IOPS SSD for demanding latency/IOPS; throughput HDD for suitable sequential workloads, not boot disks.

EBS is AZ-scoped. Snapshots are incremental backups used to restore volumes, copy across Regions and create AMIs. Quiesce application writes for consistency; Fast Snapshot Restore avoids initialization latency where configured.
Multi-Attach supports certain io1/io2 uses in one AZ and needs application/filesystem coordination. Instance store survives reboot, but not stop/termination or underlying disk loss.
lessons.decision: Persistent VM disk: EBS. Re-creatable ultra-fast scratch: instance store. Shared file semantics across AZs: EFS/appropriate FSx.
lessons.trap: Multi-Attach does not turn ordinary ext4/XFS into a safe multi-writer cluster filesystem. Increasing volume size may also require filesystem expansion.
lessons.example: A database uses durable EBS; an analytics worker uses local scratch and writes completed results to S3 before termination.
lessons.question: Why can a restored EBS volume initially feel slower?
lessons.answer: Blocks may be initialized lazily from the snapshot. Use suitable pre-initialization or Fast Snapshot Restore when needed.

lessons.title: EFS: shared Linux files
lessons.mental: EFS = shared NFS filesystem untuk banyak clients. Access point dapat memberi setiap aplikasi directory dan POSIX identity tersendiri.
core: Regional EFS supports multi-AZ access via mount targets; One Zone trades AZ resilience for cost. Security groups, IAM/file-system policies and POSIX permissions all matter.
Choose throughput mode for workload behavior: bursting, provisioned or elastic where supported. Lifecycle policies can move cold files into cheaper classes with different access costs.
EFS replication supports recovery copies; plan destination promotion, network access and actual recovery testing.
lessons.decision: Shared Linux web content or application files: EFS. Windows SMB/NTFS requirement: FSx for Windows.
lessons.trap: Throughput, IOPS and capacity are different dimensions. A read/write IAM allow cannot automatically override all filesystem permission constraints.
lessons.example: Several web servers in different AZs mount EFS; separate app access points restrict each app to its own root directory.
lessons.question: What does an EFS access point enforce?
lessons.answer: An application-specific path and optional POSIX user/group identity, combined with relevant IAM and network controls.

lessons.title: S3 objects, lifecycle & replication
lessons.mental: S3 menyimpan objects dengan keys, bukan block disk atau POSIX shared drive.
core: Select a storage class from access frequency, retrieval delay, AZ resilience and minimum storage charges. Lifecycle transitions move data by rules.

CRR and SRR copy eligible objects between versioned buckets. Replication is asynchronous; existing objects and deletion behavior require deliberate configuration. RTC provides a specified replication-time service commitment for eligible objects.
Native S3 events can go to supported destinations or EventBridge for richer routing. Consumers must handle retries/duplicates.
lessons.decision: Static assets and durable object datasets: S3. Multi-Region recovery: replication plus failover/readiness planning.
lessons.trap: S3 strong read-after-write consistency does not imply synchronous cross-Region replication. A replica bucket is not inherently read-only.
lessons.example: A photo upload emits an event, Lambda creates a thumbnail, and a separate replication rule copies eligible originals for DR.
lessons.question: Does lifecycle automatically create a second regional copy?
lessons.answer: No. Lifecycle changes storage/retention within its scope; replication creates another copy.

lessons.title: S3 performance, analytics & metadata indexes
lessons.mental: Optimalkan transfer, request distribution, dan data organization sebelum menambah compute.
core: Multipart upload parallelizes large uploads; byte-range GET parallelizes downloads or reads only a portion. Abort incomplete multipart uploads with lifecycle rules to avoid paying for abandoned parts.
Spread request load across prefixes where useful and consider KMS request capacity with SSE-KMS. Transfer Acceleration uses the edge network for suitable long-distance transfers.
Storage Class Analysis informs lifecycle choices; Storage Lens aggregates storage/activity/protection insights. A DynamoDB metadata index supports custom access patterns over uploaded objects.
lessons.decision: Need search by customer/date over object metadata: maintain an index. Need organization-wide storage visibility: Storage Lens.
lessons.trap: A filename extension filter in events is a prefix/suffix match, not an arbitrary wildcard engine. Extra prefixes do not solve a single hot object by themselves.
lessons.example: Store immutable product images in S3, metadata in DynamoDB, and deliver images through CloudFront. Query the index rather than listing every object.
lessons.question: Why delete incomplete multipart parts?
lessons.answer: They consume billable storage even though the upload never became a completed object.

lessons.title: Choose the correct FSx filesystem
lessons.mental: Nama protocol sering langsung menentukan jawaban: SMB, NFS, iSCSI, atau Lustre.
core: FSx for Windows supports SMB, NTFS/AD integration and Windows share semantics. FSx for Lustre serves parallel HPC/ML workloads and integrates with S3 datasets.
Lustre scratch is temporary; persistent deployments replicate within their deployment design. Lazy loading fetches data as needed instead of waiting for an entire dataset.
FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports NFS, SMB and iSCSI with ONTAP capabilities. OpenZFS fits NFS/ZFS workloads. Migration and resizing constraints differ by filesystem.
lessons.decision: Windows file shares: FSx Windows. Parallel analytics over S3: Lustre. Existing ONTAP/multiprotocol: ONTAP. ZFS/NFS semantics: OpenZFS.
lessons.trap: Do not apply one FSx product’s storage-resizing rules to every FSx product. For Windows downsizing, create a smaller target and migrate data.
lessons.example: A team needs AD-integrated SMB shares across AZs: select FSx Windows Multi-AZ rather than EFS or S3 alone.
lessons.question: Why use Lustre with S3 for an HPC job?
lessons.answer: It provides a high-performance parallel filesystem while S3 remains a durable dataset repository.

lessons.title: DataSync, Transfer Family & Data Exchange
lessons.mental: DataSync memindahkan data; Transfer Family melayani file-transfer clients; Data Exchange menyediakan data pihak ketiga.
core: DataSync transfers supported file/object data between locations with verification, scheduling and supported metadata preservation. Agent requirements depend on source/destination type.
Transfer Family exposes supported SFTP/FTPS/FTP interfaces backed by supported S3/EFS configurations. Endpoint type determines private/public access and network controls.
Data Exchange is for subscribing to third-party datasets or supported data products. Compare total storage cost including operations, retrieval and transfer, not only GB-month.
lessons.decision: One-time or recurring migration/synchronization: DataSync. Partners insist on SFTP: Transfer Family. Purchased external dataset: Data Exchange.
lessons.trap: SFTP and FTPS are different protocols. Moving data into S3 does not preserve every filesystem behavior for applications.
lessons.example: A supplier keeps its SFTP client while Transfer Family writes files into S3; an EventBridge-triggered pipeline processes arrivals.
lessons.question: Why not use Transfer Family for a large NFS migration by default?
lessons.answer: DataSync directly targets that transfer/synchronization job with supported verification and metadata handling; Transfer Family targets protocol-based client access.

lessons.title: CloudFront origins, failover & price classes
lessons.mental: CDN cache menaruh response dekat pengguna sehingga origin menerima lebih sedikit requests.
core: Use OAC to protect supported S3 origins. S3 website endpoints behave as custom origins and differ from private S3 REST origins. VPC origins support eligible private application origins.
Origin groups provide failover for supported methods/conditions. Cache behaviors and TTLs determine which content is cached and how long.
Price classes trade edge-location coverage for cost; geo restrictions control viewer countries, not legal proof of user residency.
lessons.decision: Global web assets: CloudFront/S3. Reduce database load only when the relevant response can be safely cached.
lessons.trap: Origin failover is not a general replay-safe failover for every POST/write. Protect origins against bypassing the CDN.
lessons.example: A product image uses a long TTL and versioned filename. Personalized account data needs an appropriate private/no-cache policy and authorization.
lessons.question: Is CloudFront replication the same as S3 CRR?
lessons.answer: No. A cache can evict data and follows TTLs; replication creates a separate durable bucket copy.

lessons.title: Signed URLs, signed cookies & errors
lessons.mental: Signed access memberi izin sementara tanpa menjadikan seluruh content publik.
core: CloudFront signed URLs/cookies are created by an authorized application using a private signing key; trusted key groups are the recommended signer-management approach.
A signed URL usually authorizes a selected resource; signed cookies help when many protected files must be accessed without changing each URL.
S3 presigned URLs instead sign S3 operations using IAM credentials. Custom error pages and error caching need suitable TTLs to avoid prolonging a recovered error.
lessons.decision: Protected video files delivered by CDN: CloudFront signed access. Direct object PUT/GET: S3 presigned URL.
lessons.trap: CloudFront signing does not require a root-managed account key pair when using trusted key groups. Signing is done by your application; not every URL requires a CloudFront API call.
lessons.example: A paid video player receives signed cookies covering its protected streaming files while the S3 origin remains private via OAC.
lessons.question: Why might users keep seeing an error after the origin recovers?
lessons.answer: CloudFront may still cache the error response according to its error caching settings.

lessons.title: CloudFront Functions vs Lambda@Edge
lessons.mental: Pilih tempat eksekusi berdasarkan event, kebutuhan network, dan kompleksitas logic.
core: CloudFront Functions handles lightweight JavaScript at viewer request/response events: normalization, redirects, simple validation and headers.
Lambda@Edge supports viewer and origin events with richer execution capabilities and supported network access. Deploy its source function in us-east-1 as required.
Viewer-request logic runs before cache lookup; origin-request logic runs when an origin fetch is needed. Cache-key design determines whether user-specific responses can be safely reused.
lessons.decision: Simple URL/header normalization: CloudFront Functions. Origin selection or logic requiring supported external calls: Lambda@Edge.
lessons.trap: Do not cache personalized content under a key shared by all users. CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge cannot both handle viewer events on the same behavior in the incompatible combination.
lessons.example: Normalize tracking query parameters out of the cache key so equivalent public image requests reuse one cached object.
lessons.question: Which event avoids running on every cache hit when only origin routing must change?
lessons.answer: An origin-request Lambda@Edge event, because it runs on requests that proceed to the origin.

lessons.title: ElastiCache & stateless applications
lessons.mental: Cache adalah salinan cepat yang boleh stale. Session store menyimpan state bersama agar app servers bisa diganti.
core: Cache-aside: check cache, read database on a miss, then populate cache. Use TTL and invalidation to manage stale data; choose a policy for cache outages.
Redis/Valkey-style capabilities include rich structures and replication options. Memcached fits simpler caching; supported durability features depend on deployment type.
Move sessions out of individual EC2 instances so any healthy instance can serve the next request. Cache is not a replacement for durable business records.
lessons.decision: General application/session cache: ElastiCache. DynamoDB-compatible read acceleration: DAX.
lessons.trap: A cache improves read latency but does not repair a poorly designed write path. Sticky sessions alone do not make session data resilient to instance loss.
lessons.example: If 80% of 1,000 requests/s hit cache, roughly 200 requests/s reach the origin under a simple independent-request model.
lessons.question: What must you design before introducing cache?
lessons.answer: Keys, TTL/invalidation, acceptable staleness, miss handling and behavior when the cache is unavailable.

lessons.title: DynamoDB: keys, indexes, streams & DAX
lessons.mental: Desain DynamoDB dimulai dari access patterns. Partition key menyebarkan data; sort key mengurutkan items dalam partition.
core: Primary keys may be partition-only or partition-plus-sort. Query uses key conditions; Scan reads broadly. LSI keeps the partition key and is created with the table; GSI supplies another key path and can be added later.
Choose on-demand or provisioned capacity. Item size is limited; transactions and consistent reads consume different capacity from basic eventual reads.
TTL removes expired items asynchronously. Streams expose changes; global tables replicate across Regions. DAX accelerates compatible reads, not writes or strongly consistent reads from cache.
lessons.decision: Predictable key-value access at scale: DynamoDB. Frequent alternative lookup: appropriate GSI. Repeated eventually consistent reads: DAX.
lessons.trap: A hot partition key can throttle even if total table capacity looks adequate. DAX does require client configuration and is not a fix for hot writes.
lessons.example: Orders use customerId as partition key and orderTimestamp as sort key; a GSI supports a separate lookup by order status if distribution is safe.
lessons.question: Can you add an LSI after table creation?
lessons.answer: No. Plan LSIs at table creation; GSIs can be added later.

lessons.title: OpenSearch: search and log analytics
lessons.mental: Search engine membangun index untuk full-text search dan analytics; biasanya bukan source of truth transaksi.
core: OpenSearch indexes documents and supports search/aggregation. Dashboards visualizes indexed data; ingestion pipelines move and transform source events.
A DynamoDB Stream plus consumer can maintain a searchable copy. CloudWatch subscriptions and supported ingestion paths supply logs.
Decide freshness, retries, replay, index mappings, retention and recovery from missed updates.
lessons.decision: Need text search/flexible document search over operational data: OpenSearch. Need primary keyed writes: DynamoDB or an appropriate transactional database.
lessons.trap: Adding a search index creates another copy that can lag. Do not promise immediate transactional consistency across database and search index.
lessons.example: The application writes an order to DynamoDB, and a stream consumer indexes it for customer-service search.
lessons.question: Which system should be authoritative for an order payment?
lessons.answer: The designed transactional system of record, not a potentially lagging search index.

lessons.title: RDS: availability, replicas & connection pooling
lessons.mental: Multi-AZ untuk availability; read replica untuk read scaling. Lihat jenis deployment sebelum menyimpulkan behavior.
core: RDS manages supported database infrastructure, backups and maintenance. Automated backups support PITR; manual snapshots have their own retention lifecycle.
Traditional Multi-AZ DB instances use a non-readable standby; read replicas asynchronously serve reads and can support DR. Multi-AZ DB clusters have a different readable-standby model.
RDS Proxy pools connections, especially valuable for bursty Lambda workloads. IAM DB authentication establishes supported database login; SQL authorization remains inside the database.
lessons.decision: Write availability in one Region: appropriate Multi-AZ deployment. Read bottleneck: replicas. Connection storms: RDS Proxy.
lessons.trap: Read replicas do not automatically fix write saturation. Cross-Region promotion is a recovery workflow. RDS for Oracle does not provide every self-managed Oracle feature, such as RAC.
lessons.example: Thousands of Lambda executions share a smaller connection pool through RDS Proxy instead of opening a separate long-lived backend connection each.
lessons.question: Does CloudTrail show every SELECT statement?
lessons.answer: No. Use appropriate database logs/auditing and performance tools for SQL-level investigation.

lessons.title: Aurora: shared storage & endpoints
lessons.mental: Aurora memisahkan compute instances dari distributed storage. Endpoints mengarahkan koneksi berdasarkan peran.
core: The writer/cluster endpoint targets the current writer. The reader endpoint balances connections among eligible replicas; custom endpoints target chosen subsets. Instance endpoints target a specific instance.
Aurora storage maintains multiple copies across AZs and supports replica failover. Reader scaling and writer capacity remain separate concerns.
Use database metrics, supported performance tools and slow-query logs to diagnose CPU, waits, connections or query issues before selecting a scaling action.
lessons.decision: Separate heavy analytics onto suitable replicas/custom endpoints. Use the writer endpoint for writes and recovery-aware connection handling.
lessons.trap: Reader endpoints balance connections, not each SQL statement. Long-lived connections may distribute unevenly. An endpoint does not enforce all SQL permissions.
lessons.example: A custom endpoint routes report connections to larger replicas while ordinary application reads use another eligible group.
lessons.question: Will adding readers necessarily accelerate slow writes?
lessons.answer: No. Diagnose the writer bottleneck; replicas primarily provide read capacity and failover options.

lessons.title: Aurora Serverless, Global Database & migration
lessons.mental: Serverless capacity scaling dan cross-Region disaster recovery adalah keputusan terpisah.
core: Aurora Serverless adapts supported compute capacity to demand; configure its bounds and check engine/version support. Data API exposes supported SQL access through HTTPS; availability is not limited to one historical Aurora mode.
Global Database uses a primary writer Region and secondary Regions for low-latency reads and DR. Write forwarding sends writes to the primary; it is not independent multi-writer conflict resolution.
Migration from supported RDS engines can use snapshots or a replica/promotion path as applicable.
lessons.decision: Variable relational workload: evaluate Serverless. Regional recovery and global reads: evaluate Global Database.
lessons.trap: Do not treat illustrative replication lag or failover time as guaranteed RPO/RTO. Test end-to-end recovery including application reconnection.
lessons.example: Singapore readers query a secondary; a write is forwarded to the primary and replicated back, so cross-Region write latency still exists.
lessons.question: Does write forwarding make a secondary an independent writer?
lessons.answer: No. The authoritative write still happens in the primary Region.

lessons.title: Step Functions: orchestration & error handling
lessons.mental: State machine menjelaskan urutan, cabang, paralelisme, retry, wait, dan hasil setiap langkah.
core: Use optimized/service SDK integrations to orchestrate work without unnecessary glue functions. Long-running jobs can use supported wait-for-completion patterns; human approvals can use callback tokens.
Standard workflows support long duration and detailed execution history. Express targets short high-volume workflows; synchronous and asynchronous Express have different execution semantics.
Set Retry with backoff, Catch for recovery, and timeouts. Alert on failed execution with EventBridge.
lessons.decision: Human approval or long orchestration: Standard. High-volume short idempotent event processing: consider Express.
lessons.trap: “Exactly once workflow execution” does not make every external side effect exactly once if a task is retried. Design task idempotency.
lessons.example: A workflow validates an order, charges payment with an idempotency key, waits for fulfillment and records failure compensation where needed.
lessons.question: Why not keep a Lambda running while waiting for approval?
lessons.answer: Lambda has an invocation time limit and consumes execution resources. A state-machine wait/callback is designed for that pause.

lessons.title: SQS: visibility, retries & idempotency
lessons.mental: Queue menyerap lonjakan. Receive menyembunyikan message sementara; Delete mengakui bahwa pekerjaan selesai.
core: Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering. Visibility timeout hides a received message while processing. If it is not deleted in time, it becomes available again.
Use long polling to reduce empty responses. A DLQ isolates repeatedly failing messages; inspect/fix before redrive. Match queue types as required.
For Lambda, event-source mapping polls the queue. Configure batch failure handling, visibility timeout and concurrency to avoid unnecessary retries and overload.
lessons.decision: Decouple a slow service with SQS and rate/concurrency-controlled workers. Use an idempotency key for payments or other side effects.
lessons.trap: An upsert is not automatically idempotent: an increment executed twice still doubles its effect. FIFO does not eliminate the need for safe retry handling.
lessons.example: Order 123 is retried after a timeout. A conditional record/check on its processing ID prevents a second charge.
lessons.question: Where does the poison-message DLQ belong for SQS-triggered Lambda?
lessons.answer: On the source SQS queue via its redrive policy, rather than relying on Lambda’s asynchronous invocation DLQ.

lessons.title: Amazon MQ: protocol compatibility
lessons.mental: MQ = managed broker untuk aplikasi yang bergantung pada broker protocols dan semantics.
core: Existing applications may rely on ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ-compatible protocols and messaging behavior such as AMQP, MQTT, STOMP or OpenWire, depending on engine.
Amazon MQ reduces broker infrastructure operations but requires engine compatibility, capacity planning and suitable HA configuration.
SQS/SNS provide highly managed cloud-native APIs and scaling, but migrating to them can require application changes.
lessons.decision: Minimum changes for a supported legacy broker workload: Amazon MQ. New cloud-native decoupling without protocol constraints: consider SQS/SNS.
lessons.trap: A managed broker is not automatically a drop-in replacement for every proprietary broker feature. Validate the required protocol and semantics.
lessons.example: A legacy application uses a supported ActiveMQ client and moves to a Multi-AZ Amazon MQ deployment after compatibility testing.
lessons.question: Why might SQS be the wrong migration answer even though it scales well?
lessons.answer: The application may require an existing broker protocol/behavior and the question may demand minimal code changes.

lessons.title: SNS fan-out, filtering & delivery failures
lessons.mental: SNS menyebarkan satu message ke banyak subscribers. SQS menyimpan pekerjaan sampai worker memprosesnya.
core: Attach a queue per independent consumer to an SNS topic. Each consumer can retry and scale independently; queue policies must allow the topic to send.
Subscription filters select relevant events. FIFO topic/queue designs provide ordering within message groups and deduplication behavior, subject to supported subscription types.
SNS delivery retries depend on endpoint type. A subscription DLQ records exhausted delivery attempts; it is distinct from the worker queue’s processing DLQ.
lessons.decision: One order needs independent fraud/shipping/accounting processing: SNS → separate SQS queues.
lessons.trap: Multiple workers on one SQS queue compete for messages; they do not each get every message. SNS without a queue is not the same durable work-buffer design.
lessons.example: Fraud delays for ten minutes while shipping continues from its own queue. Shipping does not wait for the fraud queue to drain.
lessons.question: Where is an SNS delivery DLQ attached?
lessons.answer: To a subscription. It handles delivery failures to that subscriber, not every application-processing failure after delivery.

lessons.title: Streaming: Kinesis, Firehose & Flink
lessons.mental: Stream menyimpan ordered event log untuk dibaca ulang; delivery service mengirim data ke destination; processor menghitung di atas stream.
core: Kinesis Data Streams provides replay and independent consumers, ordered within shards for a key. Provisioned shards have write-byte, write-record and read-capacity limits; hot keys can dominate one shard.
Amazon Data Firehose buffers and delivers to supported destinations, with optional transformations and format conversion. It is not a consumer replay store.
Managed Service for Apache Flink performs stateful stream computations such as event-time windows and aggregations over supported sources.
lessons.decision: Replay/multiple real-time consumers: Kinesis. Managed delivery into S3: Firehose. Stateful streaming analytics: Flink.
lessons.trap: A partition key hashes to a shard; it does not automatically create one shard per device. Firehose buffering adds latency and does not provide arbitrary historical replay.
lessons.example: With 3 MB/s writes and 4,500 small records/s, the record-rate limit can require five standard provisioned shards even when bytes alone suggest three.
lessons.question: What do you calculate before choosing shard count?
lessons.answer: At least the ceilings for write bytes, write records and read throughput, then account for skew, consumer mode and headroom.

lessons.title: Amazon MSK & Kafka compatibility
lessons.mental: MSK menjalankan managed Apache Kafka. Kafka topics terbagi menjadi partitions; consumers menggunakan offsets.
core: Choose MSK when Kafka API/client/ecosystem compatibility is a requirement. Provisioned and serverless options have different operational/capacity models.
Messages are ordered within a partition, not across every partition in a topic. Consumer groups coordinate processing; offsets support replay within retention.
Kinesis is AWS-native streaming with shards and its own APIs. Both need thoughtful key distribution, retention, security and consumer design.
lessons.decision: Existing Kafka application with minimal API changes: MSK. AWS-native stream without Kafka dependency: compare Kinesis.
lessons.trap: Adding partitions can affect key-to-partition mapping and ordering assumptions. Managed Kafka still needs a suitable topic and consumer design.
lessons.example: An existing Kafka telemetry pipeline moves to MSK while retaining compatible producers and Flink processing.
lessons.question: Kafka partition or entire topic: where is order guaranteed?
lessons.answer: Within a partition. Cross-partition global ordering requires additional application design.

lessons.title: Batch: containers for finite jobs
lessons.mental: Batch menangani job queue dan compute scheduling. Job bukan service HTTP yang harus selalu hidup.
core: Package finite jobs as container images and provide job requirements. Batch uses supported compute environments and scales resources to demand.

Managed environments handle underlying capacity choices; unmanaged environments give you greater infrastructure responsibility. EventBridge schedules jobs and Step Functions orchestrates dependencies.
Multi-node parallel jobs run tightly coupled work across supported nodes; their purchasing/environment restrictions differ from ordinary jobs.
lessons.decision: Long-running containerized batch workload: Batch. Short event handler: Lambda. Continuously running application: ECS/EKS service.
lessons.trap: The standard Lambda 15-minute limit cannot be increased just by adding memory. A Batch job still needs input access, IAM, networking and durable output handling.
lessons.example: A two-hour simulation runs in Batch, stores checkpoints/results in S3 and retries safely if its permitted compute is interrupted.
lessons.question: Why use Batch rather than a permanently idle EC2 cron server?
lessons.answer: Managed scheduling and demand-based compute can avoid idle capacity and simplify job orchestration.

lessons.title: EMR, Glue & the Data Catalog
lessons.mental: EMR memberi big-data frameworks; Glue menyiapkan data; Data Catalog menyimpan metadata dataset.
core: EMR runs frameworks such as Spark/Hadoop with suitable cluster or supported managed execution models. Primary nodes coordinate, core nodes can store HDFS data, and task nodes add processing capacity.
Use durable S3 storage for data that must survive a transient cluster. Spot fits interruption-tolerant compute tasks better than fragile stateful dependencies.
Glue ETL transforms data; crawlers discover schema/partitions; the Glue Data Catalog lets supported analytics services share metadata.
lessons.decision: Existing Spark/Hadoop ecosystem control: EMR. Managed ETL and schema cataloging: Glue.
lessons.trap: A crawler catalogs metadata; it does not automatically clean every bad record or transform all files. HDFS on a terminated cluster is not your durable archive.
lessons.example: Glue converts raw JSON to partitioned Parquet in S3 and updates a catalog that Athena uses to query the curated dataset.
lessons.question: Data Catalog or S3: which holds the actual dataset?
lessons.answer: S3 holds the data objects; the catalog stores table/schema/location metadata.

lessons.title: Redshift, Spectrum & workload management
lessons.mental: Redshift adalah analytical warehouse untuk scans, joins, dan aggregations skala besar, bukan OLTP checkout database.
