core: Columnar storage and parallel execution fit analytics. Provisioned and serverless options exist. Load data using supported bulk/streaming paths; enhanced VPC routing controls relevant COPY/UNLOAD network paths.
Spectrum queries external S3 data using catalog metadata without first loading all of it into warehouse tables.
WLM separates/prioritizes query workloads; concurrency scaling adds eligible query capacity. Cross-Region snapshots and encryption grants support recovery designs.
lessons.decision: Repeated complex analytical queries: Redshift. Occasional serverless SQL over S3: Athena. Existing warehouse plus lake query: Spectrum.
lessons.trap: A row-by-row transactional workload is not the same as a warehouse workload. The slide’s “Redshift is never serverless” comparison is outdated.
lessons.example: Short executive queries use one workload policy while large overnight analytical queries use another, reducing queue interference.
lessons.question: What problem does WLM address?
lessons.answer: It manages query queues/priorities/resources so competing workloads do not all suffer from the same scheduling policy.

lessons.title: DocumentDB & time-series data
lessons.mental: Pilih database sesuai data model dan operations, bukan hanya label “NoSQL”.
core: DocumentDB supports MongoDB-compatible document use cases, with a compatibility matrix that must be checked before migration. It is not identical to every MongoDB version/feature.
Timestream concepts include timestamped measures, dimensions, retention tiers and time-based queries. Availability differs across Timestream offerings and customer eligibility.
Model the actual reads/writes, retention, consistency, latency and licensing/operations constraints.
lessons.decision: JSON document application requiring supported MongoDB compatibility: evaluate DocumentDB. Time-series metrics: evaluate an appropriate time-series offering.
lessons.trap: “Compatible” never guarantees every driver feature, query behavior or administrative command is identical. Avoid using dated availability assumptions for new deployments.
lessons.example: Sensor records carry deviceId, timestamp and temperature; retention keeps recent data quickly accessible and older data at lower cost.
lessons.question: What must be checked before a MongoDB-to-DocumentDB migration?
lessons.answer: Supported engine/API features, drivers, indexes, queries, data types and application behavior under realistic tests.

lessons.title: Athena, QuickSight & the analytics pipeline
lessons.mental: Athena menjawab SQL; QuickSight menyajikan insights; format dan partitioning menentukan banyak biaya scan.
core: Athena queries supported data sources, commonly S3 via Glue metadata. Partition pruning, columnar formats and compression reduce unnecessary scans. Avoid many tiny files.
Federated query uses supported connectors to access other sources; results and permissions still require design.
QuickSight analyses are authoring workspaces; dashboards are published views. SPICE provides in-memory imported data, with refresh and access controls such as row/column restrictions where supported.
lessons.decision: Ad hoc SQL over logs in S3: Athena. Share business dashboards: QuickSight. Stateful stream processing before storage: Flink.
lessons.trap: A dashboard is not a security boundary by itself. Configure data permissions and row/column access; do not assume all viewers should see all source rows.
lessons.example: Convert a 1 TB CSV dataset into partitioned Parquet; a query touching a few columns in one day may scan a small fraction of the original data.
lessons.question: Why does Parquet often reduce Athena cost?
lessons.answer: Columnar reading and compression reduce bytes scanned, especially when queries select few columns and partitions.

lessons.title: CloudWatch metrics, alarms & canaries
lessons.mental: Metrics adalah angka sepanjang waktu; alarm mengevaluasi kondisi; canary mencoba perjalanan pengguna.
core: CloudWatch collects service and custom metrics. Standard EC2 monitoring differs from detailed monitoring; memory/filesystem metrics require suitable agents or custom publishing.
Alarms evaluate metric thresholds or supported expressions and invoke configured actions. Pick the statistic, period, evaluation window and missing-data behavior deliberately.
Synthetics canaries exercise APIs or web flows, identifying functional failures even when CPU and instance health look normal.
lessons.decision: Need detect a broken login or checkout: synthetic transaction. Need detect high CPU/queue age: metric alarm.
lessons.trap: A green infrastructure metric does not prove the business transaction works. A badly chosen health signal can trigger unnecessary scaling or recovery.
lessons.example: A canary signs in and loads an order page every few minutes; its failure alarm alerts responders before many customers complain.
lessons.question: Which monitoring approach detects a valid HTTP 200 page with a broken purchase flow?
lessons.answer: A synthetic workflow that actually exercises and verifies the purchase steps, not just a status-code check.

lessons.title: CloudWatch Logs: query, filter & stream
lessons.mental: Log group mengelompokkan aplikasi; log stream memisahkan producer seperti instance atau container.
core: Set retention intentionally. Logs Insights supports investigation queries; metric filters convert matching log events into numerical signals for alarms.
Subscriptions send new matching events into supported processing/delivery services. S3 export is a batch process and can lag; it is unsuitable for urgent detection.
Deploy/configure the CloudWatch Agent with Systems Manager and Parameter Store. The agent needs permissions and connectivity.
lessons.decision: Near-real-time centralized log processing: subscription. Historical archive export: export task. Count repeated errors: metric filter.
lessons.trap: Log retention is not automatically optimized for cost. Exporting to S3 does not guarantee immediate delivery or live incident response.
lessons.example: Application logs → subscription → Firehose → central S3, with a separate low-latency alert path for critical errors.
lessons.question: Metric filter versus Logs Insights?
lessons.answer: A metric filter continuously creates metrics from matching new events; Logs Insights queries stored logs for investigation/analysis.

lessons.title: EventBridge: route events by meaning
lessons.mental: Event bus menerima events; rules memilih events; targets menjalankan respons.
core: Default buses receive supported AWS events. Custom buses carry application events; partner buses integrate supported SaaS events.
Event patterns match event content. Archive/replay supports reprocessing; schema discovery/registry helps producers and consumers agree on structure.
Resource policies control cross-account event publication. The destination action may separately need an execution role or target resource policy.
lessons.decision: React to a resource change, schedule work, or centralize cross-account events: EventBridge.
lessons.trap: EventBridge routing is not a transaction across all targets. Consumers still need idempotency and a retry/failure design.
lessons.example: A new image event routes to a workflow while security findings route to a responder queue using different rules on the bus.
lessons.question: Does permission to PutEvents automatically authorize a rule to call every target?
lessons.answer: No. Target invocation permissions and any execution role must also be configured.

lessons.title: Tracing & AWS Health
lessons.mental: Trace mengikuti satu request melalui banyak services. Health event menjelaskan dampak kejadian AWS pada resources kamu.
core: Distributed tracing links spans/segments across services to show where latency or errors occur. Instrument applications and give telemetry components the required permissions.
Use supported tracing instrumentation, including OpenTelemetry where appropriate, rather than assuming old SDK/daemon guidance never changes.
AWS Health provides account/resource-specific events; EventBridge can route notifications and remediation workflows. Public service status and account-specific impact are different views.
lessons.decision: Slow request spanning API → Lambda → database: tracing. Scheduled maintenance affecting an instance: AWS Health.
lessons.trap: CloudWatch aggregates do not automatically reveal which downstream call delayed one request. An AWS Health notification does not diagnose every application bug.
lessons.example: A trace shows most latency inside an external payment API, so increasing EC2 CPU is unlikely to solve the bottleneck.
lessons.question: What does a trace add beyond average Lambda duration?
lessons.answer: It can connect the request to downstream operations and reveal which dependency or segment consumed time.

lessons.title: Elastic Beanstalk & environment deployment
lessons.mental: Beanstalk mengelola deployment environment dari application code dengan AWS resources di bawahnya.
core: A web environment uses an appropriate load-balanced or single-instance topology. A worker environment processes queued background work; long tasks should not block a web request.
You retain responsibility for application configuration, supported platform choices, security and update strategy. Beanstalk simplifies operations but does not remove them.
Blue/green uses separate environments: validate the new one, shift traffic or swap environment URLs, and retain a rollback path.
lessons.decision: A supported web application needs managed deployment with infrastructure customization: Beanstalk.
lessons.trap: Do not couple the lifetime of production data to a disposable application environment. A DNS swap still has caching/connection behavior.
lessons.example: Web requests enqueue video work; a worker environment processes it independently so user-facing latency stays low.
lessons.question: How do you safely validate a new Beanstalk release before all users see it?
lessons.answer: Deploy it to a separate environment, test it, then use the chosen traffic-shift/URL-swap procedure with a rollback plan.

lessons.title: CodeDeploy: rolling, blue/green & canary
lessons.mental: Deployment strategy menentukan seberapa besar blast radius jika release baru bermasalah.
core: In-place EC2 deployments update existing instances in batches with AppSpec lifecycle hooks. Blue/green supplies a replacement environment and shifts traffic.
Lambda deployments move alias traffic among versions; ECS deployments can create a replacement task set with controlled routing.
Canary tests a small fraction first; linear increases it in steps. Pre/post hooks and CloudWatch alarms can stop or roll back an unhealthy rollout.
lessons.decision: Low-risk release with quick reversal: blue/green or canary, provided data/schema changes remain compatible.
lessons.trap: Traffic rollback does not automatically reverse a destructive database migration. “Zero downtime” depends on health checks, capacity and compatibility.
lessons.example: Send 10% to Lambda version 2, observe error/latency alarms, then increase or roll back the alias.
lessons.question: Canary versus linear?
lessons.answer: Canary starts with a small test fraction then advances; linear increases traffic in repeated increments.

lessons.title: CloudFormation: lifecycle, drift & StackSets
lessons.mental: IaC membuat infrastructure reproducible. Stack lifecycle tetap harus melindungi data penting.
core: Templates describe resources and relationships. StackSets apply stacks across accounts/Regions; automatic organization deployment supports new accounts.

DeletionPolicy controls resource treatment on stack deletion/removal. UpdateReplacePolicy separately addresses replacement during updates. Drift detection reports supported differences from the template.
Custom resources extend provisioning through handlers. Resource import brings supported existing resources under a stack without recreation, using identifiers and required policy metadata.
lessons.decision: Same baseline across many accounts: StackSets. Protect data on deletion: appropriate retention policy. Detect manual changes: drift detection.
lessons.trap: Drift detection does not universally fix drift or inspect every property. Retain leaves the resource and its ongoing costs outside the deleted stack.
lessons.example: A production database has deliberate deletion and replacement retention policies; a security baseline is deployed to every new account with StackSets.
lessons.question: Does DeletionPolicy:Retain mean CloudFormation continues managing the resource after stack deletion?
lessons.answer: No. The resource remains, but management through that deleted stack ends.

lessons.title: Service Catalog, SAM & CDK
lessons.mental: Service Catalog membatasi pilihan provisioning; SAM mempermudah serverless; CDK menulis IaC dengan bahasa pemrograman.
core: Service Catalog portfolios expose approved products to authorized users. Launch constraints can provide controlled provisioning permissions.
SAM provides serverless resource abstractions and deployment/testing tooling, building on CloudFormation.
CDK code synthesizes CloudFormation templates; reusable constructs help package infrastructure patterns. The resulting deployed permissions and resources still need review.
lessons.decision: Pre-approved self-service infrastructure: Service Catalog. Serverless application templates: SAM. Programmatic infrastructure definitions: CDK.
lessons.trap: CDK code is not the application’s running backend by itself. A product catalog is not a replacement for organization-wide guardrails.
lessons.example: Developers launch an approved database product from a portfolio without being given unrestricted infrastructure administrator permissions.
lessons.question: What does CDK synthesize?
lessons.answer: CloudFormation templates that describe the infrastructure to deploy.

lessons.title: Systems Manager & Cloud Map
lessons.mental: SSM mengelola mesin melalui agent dan service connectivity; Cloud Map membantu aplikasi menemukan service endpoints.
core: Run Command executes commands across managed nodes. State Manager maintains desired configuration; Automation orchestrates operations; Patch Manager applies approved baselines within maintenance windows.
Session Manager offers controlled interactive access without opening inbound SSH for ordinary sessions. Managed nodes need an agent, role/activation and network access to required service endpoints.
OpsCenter collects operational issues. Cloud Map registers/discovers resource locations and health through supported DNS/API paths.
lessons.decision: Manage many hosts without SSH: Systems Manager. Dynamically discover service endpoints: Cloud Map.
lessons.trap: An installed agent alone is insufficient: verify IAM and network access. Port-forwarding/SSH session content is not recorded like ordinary shell session logs.
lessons.example: An ASG termination hook triggers cleanup through an Automation runbook, completes the lifecycle action, then permits termination.
lessons.question: Why might an EC2 instance not appear as an SSM managed node?
lessons.answer: Check agent health, instance permissions and connectivity/DNS to required Systems Manager endpoints.

lessons.title: Cost visibility, tags & recommendations
lessons.mental: Tags memberi attribution; reports memberi visibility; recommendation tools membantu menemukan pemborosan.
core: Activate relevant cost allocation tags so billing reports can use them. Consistent keys/values make cost-center analysis meaningful; tagging tools help find missing tags.
Trusted Advisor provides supported best-practice checks. Compute Optimizer focuses on resource sizing recommendations; Service Quotas manages supported quota visibility and increases.
Current support plans and included features can differ from the old comparison table. Use the current AWS support documentation for plan decisions.
lessons.decision: Who spent it: cost allocation and usage reports. Which resource is oversized: Compute Optimizer. Quota approaching limit: Service Quotas/alarms.
lessons.trap: A tag existing on a resource is not automatically an activated billing dimension. A recommendation is not proof the proposed size meets peak requirements.
lessons.example: A finance team groups spend by CostCenter and identifies a lightly used instance; operations checks peaks before resizing.
lessons.question: Does Trusted Advisor itself increase a service quota?
lessons.answer: No. Use the supported quota-request process; recommendations/monitoring and quota changes are separate.

lessons.title: Savings Plans & commitment risk
lessons.mental: Diskon commitment mengurangi harga usage yang cocok, tetapi kamu membayar commitment meskipun utilization turun.
core: Compute Savings Plans cover eligible EC2/Fargate/Lambda usage with broad flexibility. EC2 Instance Savings Plans are narrower by family/Region. RIs have service- and scope-specific attributes.
Separate baseline utilization from unpredictable bursts before committing. Eligible excess usage is billed under its applicable pricing, often On-Demand.
Dedicated Hosts address physical tenancy/license requirements; they are not merely a generic discount plan.
lessons.decision: Stable flexible compute spend: evaluate Compute Savings Plans. Short interruption-tolerant work: Spot. Uncertain usage: avoid overcommitting.
lessons.trap: A one-year discount can cost more overall if you commit to capacity/spend you will not use. Commitment is not a usage ceiling.
lessons.example: If only 40% of a fleet runs continuously, size a commitment against the defensible baseline and handle variable demand separately.
lessons.question: Does a Savings Plan stop resources once its hourly commitment is consumed?
lessons.answer: No. Additional eligible usage continues and is billed at the applicable rate.

lessons.title: S3 economics: access pattern first
lessons.mental: Storage termurah per GB belum tentu total cost termurah. Hitung retrieval, requests, transfer, dan minimum durations.
core: Standard handles frequent access. Standard-IA provides immediate access with retrieval charges. One Zone-IA fits re-creatable data where one-AZ loss is acceptable.

Glacier Instant Retrieval is immediately accessible; Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive have restore delays. Intelligent-Tiering adapts eligible objects to access patterns, with optional archive tiers that have different retrieval behavior.
Requester Pays shifts eligible request/data-download charges to the requester; the owner still pays storage.
lessons.decision: Unknown/changing access: evaluate Intelligent-Tiering. Rare archive with long restore tolerance: Deep Archive. Non-recreatable single copy: avoid relying on one AZ.
lessons.trap: Durability measures data survival; availability measures access. A design target, a contractual SLA and observed downtime are not interchangeable.
lessons.example: An auditor needs a file within seconds once a quarter: Glacier Instant Retrieval can fit better than Deep Archive despite higher storage cost.
lessons.question: Why can moving tiny short-lived files to an archive tier increase cost?
lessons.answer: Minimum billable size/duration, request overhead and retrieval fees can outweigh the lower storage rate.

lessons.title: Budgets, Cost Explorer & rightsizing
lessons.mental: Budget adalah feedback/control workflow, bukan hard real-time spending cap.
core: Budgets tracks configured cost/usage/commitment targets and sends notifications. Budget Actions can apply supported policies or stop eligible resources automatically or after approval.
Cost Explorer visualizes trends and forecasts; detailed cost/usage data supports deeper analytics. Central or member-account budget management depends on organizational ownership.
Compute Optimizer uses utilization metrics to suggest configurations. Memory-aware decisions need memory telemetry where required. Discount sharing is configurable across organization accounts.
lessons.decision: Need an alert/action on spend threshold: Budgets. Need investigate trend: Cost Explorer. Need detailed line-item analysis: cost/usage exports.
lessons.trap: Cost data is delayed. Even automated budget actions cannot guarantee spending never exceeds a threshold. Restrictive actions also need to preserve critical operations.
lessons.example: A development budget alerts the owner early and applies an approved restriction at a higher threshold; production follows a different response policy.
lessons.question: Does a budget notification itself stop EC2?
lessons.answer: No. Stopping requires a configured supported Budget Action or another explicitly designed automation.

lessons.title: The 7 Rs: choose the migration intention
lessons.mental: Migration strategy dimulai dari business value, dependencies dan constraints, bukan service favorit.
core: Retire removes what is unnecessary; retain keeps it for now. Rehost moves largely unchanged; relocate moves to a compatible infrastructure/platform environment.
Replatform introduces limited platform improvements without a full redesign. Repurchase replaces the product, often with SaaS. Refactor/re-architect changes the application design substantially.
Map dependency groups, migration waves, testing, cutover and rollback before executing.
lessons.decision: Fastest low-change server migration: rehost. Reduce database operations with limited app changes: replatform to a managed compatible engine.
lessons.trap: “Move to cloud” is not always the right outcome for every workload. Percentage cost savings in examples are not universal promises.
lessons.example: Retire an unused report server, retain a constrained mainframe, rehost an urgent app, and later refactor its batch processing.
lessons.question: Database from self-managed MySQL to RDS MySQL: which R?
lessons.answer: Typically replatform: the engine/application can remain similar while database infrastructure becomes managed.

lessons.title: Storage Gateway: file, volume or tape?
lessons.mental: Gateway mempertahankan interface yang dikenal aplikasi sambil memakai storage AWS.
core: S3 File Gateway presents NFS/SMB backed by S3 objects and caches recent data. Coordinate cache refresh when changes occur outside the gateway; independent writers need careful consistency design.
Volume Gateway exposes iSCSI block volumes. Cached mode keeps primary data in AWS with a local cache; stored mode keeps the full local dataset with cloud backups.
Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library for existing backup software. Lifecycle/archive behavior and restore steps matter.
lessons.decision: NFS/SMB-to-S3 hybrid access: File Gateway. iSCSI volumes: Volume Gateway. Existing virtual-tape workflow: Tape Gateway.
lessons.trap: S3 File Gateway is not an arbitrary POSIX filesystem over S3 with every locking/consistency behavior. Cloud-side changes may require cache refresh.
lessons.example: A branch reads a read-only file share backed by the same S3 dataset while a primary workflow writes; refresh procedures keep the branch view current.
lessons.question: Cached versus stored Volume Gateway: where is the full primary dataset?
lessons.answer: Cached: in AWS with local hot data. Stored: on premises with cloud backups.

lessons.title: Offline transfer & edge processing
lessons.mental: Jika network terlalu lambat, physical data transport bisa lebih cepat—tergantung device availability dan shipping time.
core: Estimate transfer time using bits/bandwidth and realistic utilization; include protocol overhead and competing traffic. Compare with shipping, loading and import lead times.

The slides describe Snow devices for offline migration and edge compute. Their present ordering eligibility is a separate product-lifecycle issue; do not assume every new customer can order every legacy device.
Improve transfer throughput with parallelism, appropriately batched small files and fewer local-network bottlenecks.
lessons.decision: For an exam scenario explicitly offering a supported Snow device and poor connectivity, offline transfer may fit. For a live design, verify current eligibility.
lessons.trap: 100 Mbps is megabits per second, not megabytes. A theoretical transfer estimate is a lower bound, not an operational schedule.
lessons.example: 10 TB at 100 Mbps takes about 9.26 days at perfect utilization; at 75% utilization it takes about 12.35 days, before other overhead.
lessons.question: What assumption most often makes a transfer estimate too optimistic?
lessons.answer: Treating line rate as sustained effective throughput and ignoring shared bandwidth, retries and processing time.

lessons.title: DMS, schema conversion & CDC cutover
lessons.mental: Schema conversion mengubah struktur/logic; DMS memindahkan data dan dapat mengikuti perubahan.
core: Homogeneous migration keeps the engine; heterogeneous migration may need schema conversion and application changes. SCT or supported DMS schema conversion assists, but unsupported objects require manual work.
DMS supports full load, full load plus CDC, or CDC-only for supported source/target pairs. The replication service can use supported provisioned/serverless deployment models.
Validate data, monitor replication lag, pause final writes, catch up, redirect clients and retain a rollback strategy.
lessons.decision: Minimum downtime database migration: full load plus CDC with tested cutover. Different engine: add schema/application conversion.
lessons.trap: DMS does not automatically convert every stored procedure or guarantee zero downtime. “You must create your own EC2 instance” is an oversimplification of managed replication resources.
lessons.example: Move Oracle data to a compatible Aurora design: assess/convert schema, bulk load, replicate ongoing changes, validate, then cut over.
lessons.question: When is SCT not needed just to change the hosting platform?
lessons.answer: When the database engine/schema remains compatible, such as PostgreSQL on premises to RDS PostgreSQL; still assess extensions and compatibility.

lessons.title: Disaster recovery: RPO vs RTO
lessons.mental: RPO = berapa banyak data terbaru boleh hilang. RTO = berapa lama layanan boleh berhenti.
core: Backup/restore minimizes standing infrastructure but requires restoration. Pilot light keeps essential core/data services ready; much application capacity is not yet serving.
Warm standby runs a reduced but functioning stack that scales after failure. Multi-site/active-active runs serving capacity in multiple sites with much greater data/operations complexity.
Recovery requires identity, keys, configuration, data, capacity, routing and validation—not only a copied database.
lessons.decision: Choose the least costly design that meets the stated recovery objectives, then test it end to end.
lessons.trap: Multi-AZ availability is not automatically regional disaster recovery. Replication can copy corruption; retain protected recovery points too.
lessons.example: RPO 15 minutes means losing at most roughly the permitted recent data window; RTO one hour means restoring the service within that downtime objective.
lessons.question: Pilot light versus warm standby?
lessons.answer: Pilot light keeps critical core components ready but needs more activation. Warm standby already runs the complete service at reduced scale.

lessons.title: FIS, discovery, MGN & DRS
lessons.mental: Discovery menjawab apa yang ada; migration memindahkan; DR menyiapkan pemulihan berulang.
core: Application discovery captures inventory, utilization and dependencies; Migration Evaluator supports a business case. Dependency information helps sequence migration waves.

Application Migration Service (MGN) supports rehosting servers with staging replication and cutover. Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) focuses on ongoing recovery readiness, drills, failover and failback.
Fault Injection Simulator runs controlled failure experiments with defined targets, stop conditions and monitoring.
lessons.decision: Move servers permanently: MGN. Keep recovery capability for servers: DRS. Understand dependencies first: discovery.
lessons.trap: A replication agent does not prove application recovery works. Validate boot, licenses, network, identity and business transactions in a recovery drill.
lessons.example: A team discovers app/database dependencies, rehosts them in the same wave, tests cutover, and separately maintains DRS for remaining critical on-premises systems.
lessons.question: What is the key difference between MGN and DRS?
lessons.answer: Their goal: migration/cutover versus continuous disaster-recovery readiness and recovery operations.

lessons.title: AWS Backup & immutable recovery points
lessons.mental: Backup Plan mengatur apa, kapan, berapa lama, dan ke mana backup disimpan.
core: AWS Backup centralizes supported backup workloads, schedules, retention, copies and monitoring. Tag-based assignment and organization policies help apply consistent coverage.
Cross-account and cross-Region copies improve isolation where supported; encryption permissions and service-specific feature support must be checked.

Vault Lock offers governance/compliance retention controls. The strongest compliance protection takes effect according to its configured lock process; it is not identical to a freely removable setting.
lessons.decision: Many AWS services need centrally governed backups: AWS Backup. EBS-only snapshot lifecycle automation: DLM may be sufficient.
lessons.trap: A successful backup job does not prove a successful restore. Test recovery and confirm required keys remain available.
lessons.example: A protected log/backup account receives eligible recovery copies, and scheduled restore tests verify that the data and application can actually be recovered.
lessons.question: Does deleting an encryption key help protect backups?
lessons.answer: No. Losing required key access can make encrypted recovery data unusable.

lessons.title: VPC, CIDR & route decisions
lessons.mental: VPC adalah network boundary regional; subnet berada dalam satu AZ. CIDR menentukan ukuran alamat, bukan izin akses.
core: IPv4 /n contains 2^(32−n) addresses. In an ordinary AWS IPv4 subnet, five addresses are reserved, so /26 leaves 59 assignable addresses.
A public subnet has a route to an Internet Gateway; an IPv4 instance also needs a public IPv4/EIP and permitted traffic to use that internet path.
Routes select destinations by longest-prefix match. Primary/secondary CIDR rules and allowed address ranges are more nuanced than the slide’s claim that all VPC CIDRs are immutable/private-only.
lessons.decision: Start troubleshooting with source, destination, forward route, return route and controls on both sides.
lessons.trap: All non-RFC1918 addresses are not automatically usable public addresses; reserved ranges exist. The standard 172.16/12 private range is 172.16.0.0/12.
lessons.example: 10.0.1.42 matches both 10.0.0.0/16 and 10.0.1.0/24; the /24 is more specific.
lessons.question: Does placing EC2 in a public subnet give it internet automatically?
lessons.answer: No. The instance needs an appropriate public address, routes, and security controls that allow the traffic.

lessons.title: NAT, security groups, NACLs & IPv6
lessons.mental: NAT menyediakan outbound path; SG/NACL memfilter traffic; tidak satu pun menggantikan route yang benar.
core: A conventional zonal public NAT Gateway uses an EIP in a public subnet; private-subnet default routes point to it. Design AZ failure behavior explicitly.

A NAT instance needs source/destination checking disabled and self-managed capacity/HA. SGs are stateful allow-lists on supported interfaces; NACLs are stateless ordered allow/deny rules at subnet boundaries.
For globally routed IPv6, an egress-only IGW permits outbound-initiated connectivity and return traffic. Private IPv6 address options also exist; “all IPv6 is public” is outdated.
lessons.decision: Private IPv4 internet egress: NAT path. Private IPv6 outbound-only to IPv6 internet: egress-only IGW.
lessons.trap: NAT does not permit arbitrary unsolicited inbound connections. Stateful SG return traffic still has to pass any applicable stateless NACL and route.
lessons.example: HTTPS request leaves on port 443, but a restrictive NACL also needs the appropriate ephemeral return-port path.
lessons.question: Why can adding an SG inbound allow fail to fix a connection?
lessons.answer: A route, NACL, endpoint policy, destination listener or return-path requirement can still block it.

lessons.title: Peering vs Transit Gateway
lessons.mental: Peering adalah koneksi berpasangan. Transit Gateway adalah hub routing dengan segmentation melalui route tables.
core: Peering supports non-overlapping VPC CIDRs with explicit routes; it is non-transitive. A→B and B→C does not create A→C. Peering cannot generally borrow B’s edge gateways.
Transit Gateway connects supported VPC, VPN and other attachments. Association selects the routing table used for incoming attachment traffic; propagation controls which learned routes enter tables.
Separate TGW tables can isolate production and development while sharing approved services. Central egress also needs symmetric routes and proper NAT/inspection paths.
lessons.decision: Few simple VPC pairs: peering. Many VPCs/hybrid transit/central egress: TGW.
lessons.trap: Adding an attachment does not mean every network should talk to every other. Overlapping CIDRs are a routing problem, not solved by adding more peering.
lessons.example: Prod attachments use a table containing prod and approved shared services; dev routes are absent or blackholed as designed.
lessons.question: What is the difference between TGW association and propagation?
lessons.answer: Association chooses the table an attachment uses to route incoming traffic; propagation adds its learned routes to selected tables.

lessons.title: Endpoints, PrivateLink & private service access
lessons.mental: Private connectivity mengatur jalur; IAM dan resource policies tetap mengatur izin.
core: Gateway endpoints serve S3/DynamoDB through route tables inside the VPC; they cannot simply be extended through peering, TGW, VPN or DX.
Interface endpoints use ENIs/private addresses and security groups. Private DNS lets supported standard service names resolve privately. On-premises clients need routing and suitable DNS resolution.
PrivateLink exposes supported services without full network peering; the classic customer endpoint-service pattern uses a provider NLB. Endpoint policies further restrict allowed access.
lessons.decision: Private S3 from EC2 in its VPC: gateway endpoint. On-premises private S3 access via DX: suitable S3 interface endpoint/DNS.
lessons.trap: An endpoint policy does not grant permissions missing from IAM/resource policies. Restricting one endpoint does not automatically forbid every alternate access path.
lessons.example: A provider publishes an NLB-backed service; customers create interface endpoints and consume it without sharing all their network routes.
lessons.question: Why can a perfectly routed endpoint request return AccessDenied?
lessons.answer: The caller policy, endpoint policy, resource policy or KMS permission can still reject the action.

lessons.title: Site-to-Site VPN, Client VPN & hybrid routes
lessons.mental: Site-to-Site menghubungkan networks; Client VPN menghubungkan pengguna/perangkat.
core: Managed Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec tunnels and supported VGW/TGW termination. Customer gateway configuration represents the on-premises side. BGP can exchange routes dynamically.
Use both tunnels and redundant customer-side/network paths where objectives require it. Two tunnels do not eliminate every single point of failure.
Client VPN uses client authentication plus authorization rules, routes and associated networks. Access to peered/transit/on-premises networks needs a complete path and permissions.
lessons.decision: Office/data-center network to AWS: Site-to-Site VPN. Employee laptop access: Client VPN.
lessons.trap: VPN connectivity does not automatically authorize every destination. Legacy “one VPN per VPC” diagrams are not the only design; TGW provides modern transit options.
lessons.example: An employee uses Client VPN into an access VPC, then approved TGW routes reach a corporate application over hybrid connectivity.
lessons.question: Does BGP encrypt traffic?
lessons.answer: No. BGP exchanges routing information; IPsec supplies VPN encryption.

lessons.title: Direct Connect: VIFs, encryption & resilience
lessons.mental: Direct Connect memberi dedicated connectivity. Private bukan otomatis encrypted, dan satu link bukan HA.
core: Public VIF reaches supported public AWS services. Private VIF reaches VPC resources through suitable VGW/DX gateway design. Transit VIF connects through DX gateway to TGW.
DX gateway supports cross-Region/account connectivity patterns. SiteLink can connect supported DX locations without routing through an AWS Region.

LAG combines compatible connections but shared-location/device failures remain. Use diverse connections/locations and an appropriate backup path. Encryption options depend on design, such as VPN overlays or supported MACsec.
lessons.decision: Consistent hybrid bandwidth/private path: DX. Rapid setup/encrypted internet path: VPN. Many VPCs: DX gateway plus TGW as appropriate.
lessons.trap: A LAG at one facility does not protect against losing that facility. An under-sized VPN backup may not meet production throughput during a DX outage.
lessons.example: Two independent DX locations protect against location loss; a tested VPN backup offers another path with explicitly understood capacity.
lessons.question: Public VIF means traffic traverses the public internet—true or false?
lessons.answer: False. It reaches public AWS service addresses over Direct Connect; “public” describes the destinations, not an ordinary internet transport path.

lessons.title: Flow Logs & network troubleshooting
lessons.mental: Flow Logs adalah metadata koneksi, bukan isi paket atau HTTP request body.
core: Inspect source/destination addresses, ports, protocol, action and logging status. Query logs in CloudWatch or S3/Athena and identify which interface produced the record.
An ACCEPT says relevant filtering permitted that flow at the recorded point; it does not prove application success or every downstream hop accepted it.
Compare forward and return paths. Stateful SGs and stateless NACLs explain many asymmetric failures, but logs alone may not uniquely identify the rejecting rule.
lessons.decision: Need traffic metadata investigation: Flow Logs. Need API caller history: CloudTrail. Need packet payload: another appropriately authorized packet-analysis approach.
lessons.trap: Do not infer an unsolicited internet connection reached a private instance just because a NAT-interface log says ACCEPT. Inspect the complete path.
lessons.example: Requests reach the server but responses are rejected at a subnet boundary: examine outbound/return NACL rules and ephemeral ports.
lessons.question: Can Flow Logs tell you the SQL query inside an encrypted database connection?
lessons.answer: No. They capture network flow metadata, not decrypted application content.

lessons.title: Network Firewall & centralized inspection
lessons.mental: Inspection hanya berlaku untuk traffic yang benar-benar dirutekan melalui firewall.
core: AWS Network Firewall supports stateful/stateless filtering and intrusion-prevention capabilities for designed VPC paths. Rules can inspect supported protocols/domains/patterns.
Central inspection architectures use TGW, inspection subnets/endpoints and route tables to cover east-west and north-south traffic. Maintain symmetric flows and correct AZ routing.
Firewall Manager centralizes supported policies; GWLB can support third-party appliance fleets when that is the requirement.
lessons.decision: Managed VPC traffic inspection: Network Firewall. Existing third-party inspection appliances: GWLB pattern. HTTP-specific protection: WAF.
lessons.trap: Creating a firewall endpoint without updating routes leaves traffic uninspected. Stateful appliances can fail when return traffic takes a different path.
lessons.example: App VPC → TGW → inspection VPC → egress VPC → internet, with corresponding return routes through the intended inspection path.
lessons.question: East-west versus north-south?
lessons.answer: East-west is lateral workload/network traffic; north-south crosses an environment boundary, such as internet or on-premises ingress/egress.

lessons.title: Bedrock: foundation models, RAG & tuning
lessons.mental: RAG memberi model konteks saat menjawab; fine-tuning mengubah model melalui training. Jangan samakan keduanya.
core: Bedrock provides access to supported foundation models and managed generative-AI application capabilities. Model/provider/Region features differ.

Knowledge bases retrieve relevant external content for grounded responses. Agents coordinate tools; guardrails add supported policy/safety checks. Authorization to retrieve data or call a tool still needs explicit design.
Fine-tuning/customization applies only to supported models/configurations. A standard inference call does not imply a private fine-tuned copy of every model is created for you.
lessons.decision: Questions over changing company documents: RAG. A supported systematic behavior/style adaptation: evaluate fine-tuning.
lessons.trap: Retrieved text is not inherently trustworthy and a model response is not guaranteed correct. Do not grant an agent broad permissions just because the model is managed.
lessons.example: An employee assistant retrieves only documents that employee may access and cites them; tool calls use a narrowly scoped execution identity.
lessons.question: RAG or fine-tuning when a policy document changes daily?
lessons.answer: Usually RAG with updated retrieval data, because the information can change without retraining model weights.

lessons.title: Managed AI: images, speech & language
lessons.mental: Pilih dari jenis input dan output, bukan menebak dari nama service.
core: Rekognition analyzes images/video; Textract specializes in document text/forms/tables. Transcribe turns speech into text; Polly turns text into speech, with lexicons/SSML for pronunciation and prosody.
Translate translates language; Comprehend extracts language insights such as entities/sentiment. Comprehend Medical targets supported clinical-text analysis.
Lex handles conversational intent; Connect manages contact-center workflows. Confidence thresholds and human review help manage uncertain model outputs.
lessons.decision: Image labels: Rekognition. Audio transcript: Transcribe. Spoken output: Polly. Translation: Translate. Entities/sentiment: Comprehend.
lessons.trap: A confidence score is not proof. Supported languages/features differ, and automatic PII detection may miss data.
lessons.example: A call pipeline uses Connect, Transcribe, Comprehend and an approved response workflow; Lex handles a constrained appointment intent.
lessons.question: Does Polly transcribe a customer’s call?
lessons.answer: No. Polly is text-to-speech; Transcribe is speech-to-text.

lessons.title: SageMaker, Kendra, Personalize & Textract
lessons.mental: Custom model development berbeda dari memakai service AI untuk tugas yang sudah umum.
core: SageMaker AI supports building, training and deploying ML models with model/data operations responsibilities.
Kendra supports enterprise document search across supported sources. Personalize provides recommendation workflows based on relevant interaction/catalog data.
Textract extracts document text and structured elements such as forms/tables; downstream validation converts extraction into reliable business data.
lessons.decision: Build a custom predictive model: SageMaker. Enterprise document search: Kendra. Recommendations: Personalize. Invoice extraction: Textract.
lessons.trap: Do not train a custom model when a supported managed task service meets the requirement with less effort. Extraction alone does not validate invoice arithmetic.
lessons.example: Textract reads an invoice; application rules validate totals; ambiguous fields go to human review before accounting approval.
lessons.question: Kendra or Personalize for recommending the next product?
lessons.answer: Personalize. Kendra is focused on retrieving information from indexed enterprise content.

lessons.title: CI/CD: source, build, approve, deploy
lessons.mental: CI menguji integrasi perubahan. Continuous delivery menjaga software siap dirilis; deployment policy menentukan kapan release berjalan.
core: CodePipeline orchestrates stages. CodeBuild compiles/tests/packages. CodeDeploy handles supported deployments; CloudFormation provisions infrastructure. ECR stores container images.
Connect source repositories through supported connections/integrations. Add manual approvals where governance requires a human gate.
Build once, promote the tested artifact, protect credentials and restrict pipeline roles. Security scanning does not replace least privilege or secret rotation.
lessons.decision: Need coordinate source→test→approval→deployment: CodePipeline. Need run tests/build image: CodeBuild.
lessons.trap: A passing unit test is not proof of production compatibility. The deck’s “CodeBuild has no time limit” should not be memorized as a universal quota claim.
lessons.example: A pipeline tests code, builds an immutable image, pushes it to ECR, waits for production approval and deploys it with monitored rollback.
lessons.question: Does CodePipeline itself compile your application?
lessons.answer: It orchestrates a build action such as CodeBuild; the build service performs compilation/tests.

lessons.title: Contact flows & video streams
lessons.mental: Video stream dan metadata event stream mempunyai fungsi dan consumers berbeda.
core: Kinesis Video Streams ingests/stores supported video streams for playback/processing. Video producers and parser/consumer integrations differ from ordinary Kinesis Data Streams.
A video-analysis pipeline can produce detection metadata into a data stream for analytics, without treating raw video as ordinary tiny event records.
Lex and Connect provide conversational/contact-center workflows. Some adjacent products pictured in older diagrams have retired or changed; focus on the current supported components.
lessons.decision: Need ingest camera video: Kinesis Video Streams. Need stream small detection events: Kinesis Data Streams.
lessons.trap: A video-stream service does not automatically export every raw clip to your own S3 bucket in the shown pattern. Design the required extraction/archive path.
lessons.example: Cameras send video; analysis emits event metadata; dashboards aggregate detections without repeatedly scanning all video bytes.
lessons.question: Why keep detection metadata separate from raw video?
lessons.answer: It makes real-time event processing/search smaller and faster while video retention/playback follows its own storage workflow.

lessons.title: WorkSpaces, AppStream & Device Farm
lessons.mental: Desktop, application streaming, dan testing devices adalah tiga kebutuhan berbeda.
core: WorkSpaces provides managed virtual desktop experiences with identity/network and lifecycle choices. Availability/DR needs user-state and directory planning, not just an alternate endpoint.
AppStream 2.0 streams supported applications to users, commonly through a browser, reducing client installation requirements.
Device Farm tests applications on supported real devices/browsers and produces testing evidence. WorkSpaces IP access controls restrict permitted connection sources.
lessons.decision: Managed employee desktop: WorkSpaces. Stream a specific desktop application: AppStream. Cross-device app testing: Device Farm.
lessons.trap: Older WorkSpaces diagrams may reference retired components such as WorkDocs/WAM. Treat them as historical; validate current persistence/application-management choices.
lessons.example: A contractor needs one GPU application from a browser: AppStream may fit better than providing a full persistent employee desktop.
lessons.question: Which service helps test a mobile app on real devices?
lessons.answer: AWS Device Farm.

lessons.title: Macie, SES & campaign messaging
lessons.mental: Macie mencari sensitive data di S3; SES mengirim email; campaign orchestration memilih audience dan journey.
core: Macie inspects supported S3 data for sensitive information and reports findings; it is not a universal scanner for every database.
SES supports transactional/bulk email workflows, deliverability feedback and authentication mechanisms such as DKIM/SPF. Configuration sets route events/metrics and organize sending behavior.
The slides describe Pinpoint for targeted campaigns. Product lifecycle and successor choices must be checked before a new design. SNS and SES alone do not supply every campaign-management feature.
lessons.decision: Sensitive-data discovery in S3: Macie. Application email: SES. Event fan-out: SNS.
lessons.trap: Finding PII does not automatically redact or delete it. Sending an email is not the same as designing a segmented customer campaign.
lessons.example: SES sends a receipt; a configuration-set event records delivery/bounce information; the application updates contact status through its approved workflow.
lessons.question: Macie or Inspector for credit-card numbers in S3 documents?
lessons.answer: Macie. Inspector targets supported workload vulnerabilities rather than document PII discovery.

lessons.title: Image Builder & IoT Core
lessons.mental: Image Builder membuat machine/container image yang diuji; IoT Core menerima device messages dan merutekannya.
core: Image Builder pipelines build, test and distribute approved AMIs/images across supported accounts/Regions. Rollout to existing instances still needs a deployment/refresh step.
IoT Core provides device connectivity, authentication, publish/subscribe messaging and rules that send data to supported services.
Separate device identity, ingestion, transformation, storage and analytics. Device-side buffering/offline behavior remains part of the application design.
lessons.decision: Repeated golden-AMI maintenance: Image Builder. Fleet of connected device messages: IoT Core.
lessons.trap: Creating a new AMI does not update every running EC2 instance. An IoT rule does not eliminate downstream quotas or error handling.
lessons.example: IoT messages route into Firehose for S3 storage; a separate Image Builder pipeline patches and validates the analytics worker AMI.
lessons.question: How does a new AMI reach existing ASG instances?
lessons.answer: Update the launch template and perform a controlled instance refresh or other deployment process.

lessons.title: Sample cases: governance, vendor roles & CORS
lessons.mental: Tiga pola awal: hormati account autonomy, gunakan machine roles, dan pahami browser cross-origin checks.
core: Slides 771–776 choose billing alerts under the constraint that business groups retain control. Alerts improve detection; they do not enforce a hard spending cap.
Slides 777–783 use StackSets to place vendor-trusted roles in each required account. A single role in the management account does not automatically confer access to all member resources.
Slides 784–787 require the browser-facing API to permit the page’s origin. The source’s static-website setup is one hosting architecture, not the only way S3 objects can serve a page.
lessons.decision: Read the exact question constraints before applying a general best practice from another scenario.
lessons.trap: These are supplied worked examples, not evidence of questions on your actual exam. Some old explanations simplify or overstate current behavior.
lessons.example: Explain why “put all IAM users in a group” misses roles/root and why a vendor should assume scoped roles instead of sharing a workforce password.
lessons.question: What two permission relationships matter for vendor cross-account monitoring?
lessons.answer: The vendor must be allowed to assume each target role, and each target role needs the necessary read permissions; include a suitable ExternalId condition.

lessons.title: Sample cases: diagnosis, SSM & role placement
lessons.mental: Pisahkan symptom dari root cause. Letakkan role pada account tempat izin itu perlu dijalankan.
core: Slides 788–794 associate burst failures with Lambda concurrency among their choices. In real diagnosis, a 502 does not uniquely identify throttling: inspect invocation errors, malformed responses and integration logs.
Slides 795–800 select Systems Manager to administer a fleet without opening extra inbound SSH ports.
Slides 801–805 place the production role in the production account, trust an authorized source, and let only operators assume it. IAM groups do not contain users from another account.
lessons.decision: Use the evidence supplied by a scenario, but do not memorize “502 always means increase concurrency.”
lessons.trap: An admin role in the wrong account does not move its permissions to a different account. Trust policy and identity permissions are complementary.
lessons.example: Developers operate only in Dev; operators share the same home identity but assume a production role when approved.
lessons.question: Why is Run Command compatible with blocked inbound SSH?
lessons.answer: The managed agent communicates with Systems Manager through outbound service connectivity, with suitable IAM permissions.

lessons.title: Sample cases: bottlenecks & modernization
lessons.mental: Scaling satu tier dapat merusak tier berikutnya. Hitung demand lalu lindungi bottleneck.
core: Slides 806–810 replace mostly idle workers with Lambda and consolidate stream capacity within per-shard peak limits. Remember that partition keys hash into shards, not one automatic shard per device.
Slides 811–814 buffer affiliate requests with SQS and constrain consumer concurrency. An asynchronous Lambda call alone can still overwhelm the affiliate.
Slides 815–818 choose managed database/load-balancing improvements while respecting Windows/Arm compatibility. The source skips the label “Question 9”; pages are not missing here.
lessons.decision: Protect downstream limits with queues and concurrency/rate control; modernize toward managed services when constraints allow.
lessons.trap: Concurrency is not a precise requests-per-second limiter if durations vary. Use explicit rate limiting when the downstream contract is rate-based.
lessons.example: If each worker takes 0.5 s and sends one request, concurrency 10 implies about 20 requests/s on average—not a strict upper-bound SLA.
lessons.question: Why does adding Lambda between a scalable app and an external API not automatically solve overload?
lessons.answer: Lambda can scale too. Add a buffer and deliberately bound processing rate/concurrency to the dependency’s capacity.

lessons.title: Final revision & readiness
lessons.mental: Selesai membaca bukan sama dengan bisa menjawab. Readiness terlihat dari recall, explanation, dan timed practice.
core: Use the seven-day route for a complete content pass, then spend the remaining days on mixed scenarios, error review and a realistic timed practice session.
For every mistake, record whether it came from missing knowledge, misread constraints, calculation, or choosing a working but less suitable option.
Certification-path slides are career context, not a reason to learn unrelated certifications during the last days before this exam. Prioritize weak mechanisms in this deck.
lessons.decision: Aim to explain a choice and reject its closest alternative without notes. Use fresh official practice to assess readiness.
lessons.trap: The site’s XP and raw practice percentage are learning indicators, not AWS scaled scores or a guarantee of passing.
lessons.example: Before the exam, redraw cross-account trust, hybrid DNS, a queue-buffered service and a DR plan from memory.
lessons.question: What should you write in a mistake note?
lessons.answer: The decisive constraint, the correct mechanism, why your chosen option failed, and one cue that will help you recognize the pattern next time.
